DAMGHANI:v1p468/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r18.claim: Al-nās can mean all people, as in the general address to humanity.
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r18.anchor: الثامن الناس جميع الناس قوله تعالى في سورة الحج يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم مثلها في سورة الحجرات ولقمان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: قبائل is the broken plural of قبيلة on the فعائل pattern, a standard plural for four-letter feminine فعيلة nouns such as صحيفة and كتيبة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وقبيلة وقبائل وكتيبة وكتائب وسفينة وسفائن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Four-letter فعال nouns take أفعلة for the smaller count and often فعل for larger numbers; Tamim may lighten the latter, and speakers sometimes use the smaller pattern for larger counts.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: أما ما كان فعالا فإنك إذا كسرته على بناء أدنى العدد كسرته على أفعلة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Geminate فعال nouns usually stop at the smaller-count plural because further pluralization would repeat the difficult doubled consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وأما ما كان منه مضاعفا فإنهم لم يجاوزوا به أدنى العدد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: فعال nouns with weak yāʾ or wāw also avoid the larger plural pattern because the resulting weak consonants combine heavily with adjacent vowels.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وأما ما كان منه من بنات الياء والواو فإنهم لا يجاوزون به بناء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Hollow-wāw فعال forms take أفعلة for the smaller plural and a lightened فعل for larger numbers, avoiding consecutive ḍammas; a yāʾ in the corresponding position may be geminated.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: فإذا أردت بناء أكثر العدد لم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: بعض العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Yunus reports that some Arabs say صَيود/صَيْد and بيوض/بيض, extending the same lightened pattern as رسل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وزعم يونس أن من العرب من يقول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Four-letter فعَال nouns pattern like فعال: أفعلة is the smaller plural and فعل the larger, though speakers sometimes retain the smaller form for larger counts; weak forms avoid the larger plural.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: ذلك قولك زمان وأزمنة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Four-letter فِعال nouns use أفعلة for smaller counts and فعلان for larger counts; غلام has غلمان, while three غلمة makes أغلمة unnecessary, as فتية does for أفتاء.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: يقولوا أغلمة استغنوا بقولهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Geminate فِعال forms make أذبة for smaller counts and ذبان for larger ones; related nouns such as حوار form حيران, with some analogical variants and occasional retention of the smaller form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وقالوا في المضاعف حين أرادوا بناء أدنى العدد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: فعِيل takes several plural patterns: أفعلة for the smaller count, فعل, and sometimes أفعلاء; the rare فعلان pattern is analogized to فعال.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وأما ما كان فعيلا فإنه في بناء أدنى العدد بمنزلة فعال وفعال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Weak فعيل forms can use أفعلة and فعلان; صبي takes صبيان rather than أصبية because صبية already serves, and doubled forms follow the comparable regular pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وقالوا صبي وصبيان كظلمان ولم يقولوا أصبية استغنوا بصبية عنها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: فصيل forms فصال by analogy with ظريف/ظراف because the noun also functions as a quality; its feminine فصيلة reinforces the adjectival pattern, alongside forms such as أفيل/أفائل and إفال.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: فصيل حيث قالوا فصيلة كما قالوا ظريفة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Feminine four-letter nouns of these patterns use أفعل for the smaller plural and may use فعول for a collective; Sībawayh explains the split as distinguishing masculine from feminine forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وأما ما كان من هذه الأشياء الأربعة مؤنثا فإنهم إذا كسروه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Feminine forms vary: ألسن is used when اللسان is feminine and ألسنة when masculine; ذراع takes أذرع, شمال takes أشمل/شمائل or شمل, and عقاب, كراع, أتان, and يمين have their cited plural patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: من أنث اللسان فهو يقول ألسن ومن ذكر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: فعول behaves like فعيل for the smaller plural, has فعلان for larger counts, and may also use فعل or other attested patterns; wāw-final forms avoid some patterns because of the preceding kasra.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وأما ما كان فعولا فهو بمنزلة فعيل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Four-letter فعلى أفعل forms pluralize on فعل, as in الصغرى/الصغر and الكبرى/الكبر; this pattern distinguishes them from other forms and can also take sound plural suffixes.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وأما ما كان عدة حروفه أربعة أحرف وكان فعلى أفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Words ending in feminine alif drop that ending and take فعالى, often replacing yāʾ with alif; variants such as صحارى/صحار and حذف of the earlier alif distinguish the form from similar nonfeminine nouns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: للتأنيث ويبنى على فعالى وتبدل من الياء الألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Feminine nouns with فعيلة and tāʾ usually pluralize as فعائل; a few also use فعل, and sound feminine plurals remain possible for smaller counts. Weak forms include صفايا and مطايا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وذا أكثر من أن يحصى وربما كسروه على فعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: فعالة, فعالة, فعالة, and فعولة forms generally follow the same broken-plural scheme as فعيلة because their syllable count and long-vowel augmentation correspond; feminine sound plurals are also used.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: حمامة وحمائم ودجاجة ودجائج والتاء أمرها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Collective nouns on patterns such as فعال and فعيل can have a singular on the same pattern with feminine tāʾ; these behave like three-letter forms, though broken plurals are also attested.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: وقالوا دجاج كما قالوا طلحة وطلاح وجذبة وجذاب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Unaugmented masculine quadriliteral nouns pluralize on مفاعل, and forms with a fourth long-vowel letter on مفاعيل; even smaller counts do not trigger deletion of a root consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: ضفدع وضفادع وحبرج وحبارج وخنجر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Three-root nouns augmented to a four-letter shape, plus forms with non-length additions, generally pluralize on مفاعل; four-letter forms ending in a long vowel take مفاعيل, and geminates may avoid doubling.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: كل شيء كان من بنات الثلاثة فلحقته الزيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.claim: Nouns on فاعل or فاعل take فواعل and sometimes فعلان; originally adjectival forms treated as nouns favor فعلان or فعال, avoiding فواعل unless the form is restricted to men and cannot be confused with its feminine.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكسيرماعدةحروفهأربعةأحرف.anchor: تابل وتوابل وطابق وطوابق وحاجر وحواجر

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.claim: Rāzī connects the verse to the preceding rules: faulting or deriding someone for religious difference is permitted, while doing so for other reasons is forbidden under the preceding prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r1.anchor: السخرية من الغير والعيب إن كان بسبب التفاوت في الدين والإيمان ، فهو جائز لما بينا

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.claim: Apart from faith and disbelief, people share the grounds used for worldly boasting: wealth and lineage can belong to either rich or poor, believer or unbeliever, so these do not establish superiority without piety.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r2.anchor: الناس بعمومهم كفارا كانوا أو مؤمنين يشتركون فيما يفتخر

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.claim: One reading is that all people were created from Adam and Eve, so no one should boast over another as all descend from the same two parents.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : من آدم وحواء ثانيهما : كل واحد منكم أيها الموجودون

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.claim: The alternative is that each person addressed was created from a father and mother, emphasizing that all belong to the same human kind.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r4.anchor: كل واحد منكم أيها الموجودون وقت النداء خلقناه من أب وأم

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.claim: Rāzī says faith and disbelief produce a profound moral distinction, comparing the unbeliever to livestock or worse and describing the believer as truly human, while all remain one bodily kind.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#2/r5.anchor: لأن الكافر جماد إذ هو كالأنعام ، بل أضل ، والمؤمن إنسان في المعنى الذي ينبغي أن يكون فيه

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r1.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r1.claim: An objection says lineage has customary and legal weight, including a restriction on a noblewoman marrying a Nabati.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r1.anchor: فإن قيل هذا مبني على عدم اعتبار النسب ، وليس كذلك فإن للنسب اعتبارا عرفا وشرعا

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r2.claim: Rāzī answers that when religious and divine honor appears, worldly rank by lineage or wealth loses standing, as a great light or sound overwhelms lesser ones.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r2.anchor: إذا جاء الشرف الديني الإلاهي ، لا يبقى الأمر هناك اعتبار ، لا لنسب ولا لنشب

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r3.claim: Religious offices such as judgeship and testimony suit any learned, righteous person of high or low status; a profligate is unfit even with Qurashi lineage or great wealth.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r3.anchor: يصلح للمناصب الدينية كالقضاء والشهادة كل شريف ووضيع إذا كان دينا عالما صالحا

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r4.claim: If two people share strong religion, lineage can favor one in people's eyes, but not before God, since inherited nobility is not earned through effort.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r4.anchor: إذا اجتمع في اثنين الدين المتين ، وأحدهما نسيب ترجح بالنسب عند الناس لا عند الله

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r5.claim: Rāzī says lineage is singled out among worldly boasts because it is the highest and most stable: wealth can be gained by the poor, and beauty or age do not last.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r5.anchor: النسب أعلاها / لأن المال قد يحصل للفقير فيبطل افتخار المفتخر به ، والحسن والسن

RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r6.claim: Creation from the same parents and by the same Creator rules out superiority based on origin or maker; only qualities acquired after birth, especially piety and nearness to God, can distinguish people.
RAZI-FULL:v28p117#3/r6.anchor: لا ترجيح فيما خلقتم منه لأنكم كلكم من ذكر وأنثى ، ولا بالنظر إلى جاعلين لأنكم كلكم خلقكم الله

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r1.claim: One reading distinguishes dispersed peoples whose common ancestor is unknown, such as non-Arabs, from tribes joined by a known ancestor, such as Arabs and Israelites.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r1.anchor: متفرقة لا يدري من يجمعكم كالعجم

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r2.claim: Another reading treats the groups as nested ranks: tribes contain peoples, then clans, subdivisions, branches, and relatives.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r2.anchor: فإن القبيلة تحتها الشعوب ، وتحت الشعوب البطون وتحت البطون الأفخاذ

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r3.claim: One proposed purpose of peoplehood and tribes is mutual support rather than boasting.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r3.anchor: أن فائدة ذلك التناصر لا التفاخر

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r4.claim: Rāzī also reads the purpose as mutual recognition rather than estrangement, since mockery, faulting, and backbiting lead to estrangement.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r4.anchor: أن فائدته التعارف لا التناكر ، واللمز والسخرية والغيبة تفضي إلى التناكر لا إلى التعارف

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r5.claim: Creation is the foundation and tribal grouping a later state: people are created for worship and grouped for recognition, so lineage is considered only after worship matters.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r5.anchor: لأن الخلق أصل تفرع عليه الجعل { شعوبا } فإن الأول هو الخلق والإيجاد

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r6.claim: Because neither birth nor tribal assignment comes from people's effort or power, boasting over either is unjustified.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى عدم جواز الافتخاز لأن ذلك ليس لسعيكم ولا قدرة لكم على شيء من ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r7.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r7.claim: An objection notes that guidance and error are also attributed to God, citing that He guides whom He wills and has shown people the way.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r7.anchor: فإن قيل الهداية والضلال كذلك لقوله تعالى : { إنا هديناه السبيل } ( الإنسان : 3 ) { نهدى به من نشاء } ( الشورى : 52 )

RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r8.claim: Rāzī replies that guidance includes human acquisition based on action, as shown by the choice to take a path to one's Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v28p118/r8.anchor: فنقول أثبت الله لنا فيه كسبا مبنيا على فعل ، كم قال الله تعالى : { فمن شاء اتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا }

RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r1.claim: Although human willing remains subject to God's will, lineage itself involves no comparable choice or acquisition.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r1.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله } وأما في النسب فلا

RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r2.claim: The purpose of knowing one another implies a greater reason to know God: people boast about nearness to a noble ancestor, but God is the noblest being and the worthiest source of honor.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r2.anchor: إنكم جعلتم قبائل لتعارفوا وأنتم إذا كنتم أقرب إلى شريف تفتخرون به فخلقكم لتعرفوا ربكم

RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r3.claim: Pride through ancestry either regresses through ancestors or rests on an ancestor's acquired virtue; in the latter case a learned, generous person can surpass the ancestor and has no reason to boast of descent.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r3.anchor: فإن كان بالانتساب لزم الانتهاء ، وإن كان بالاكتساب فالدين الفقيه الكريم المحسن صار مثل من يفتخر به المفتخر

RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r4.claim: Rāzī allows that descent from the Prophet is uniquely honorable because no one matches his virtue, then reports the sayings that prophets leave no inheritance while scholars inherit them, interpreting this as acquired rather than genealogical inheritance.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r4.anchor: فقال : ( نحن معاشر الأنبياء لا نورث ) . وقال : ( العلماء ورثة الأنبياء ) أي لا نورث بالانتساب ، وإنما نورث بالاكتساب

RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r5.claim: Rāzī recounts hearing of a Khorasani aristocrat descended closely from Ali who was profligate, while a Black freedman advanced through knowledge and good works; the aristocrat insulted him, and the scholar answered that moral conduct made people honor him as the Prophet's heir.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r5.anchor: سمعت أن بعض الشرفاء في بلاد خراسان كان في النسب أقرب الناس إلى علي عليه السلام غير أنه كان فاسقا

RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r6.claim: The anecdote's punchline is that the scholar's inner virtue outweighed his black appearance, while people saw the aristocrat's vice rather than his ancestry and treated each by the character he displayed.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119/r6.anchor: يا أيها الشريف بيضت باطني وسودت باطنك ، فيرى الناس بياض قلبي فوق سواد وجهي

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r1.claim: Rāzī reports two directions of implication: greater piety brings greater honor, or being more honored by God produces greater piety.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r1.anchor: من يكون أتقى يكون عند الله أكرم أي التقوى تفيد الإكرام

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r2.claim: The alternative says that whoever is more honored by God is more pious, so divine honor causes piety.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r2.anchor: من يكون أكرم عند الله يكون أتقى أي الإكرام يورث التقوى

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r3.claim: The first reading is better known, though Rāzī calls the second more apparent in wording; his example, tastier foods being sweeter, makes honor proportional to piety and establishes piety's priority over other virtues.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r3.anchor: الأول أشهر والثاني أظهر لأن المذكور ثانيا ينبغي أن يكون محمولا على المذكور أولا في الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that one jurist is harder for Satan to overcome than a thousand worshippers.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r4.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لفقيه واحد أشد على الشيطان من ألف عابد )

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r5.claim: Piety is the fruit of knowledge, as 35:28 says scholars fear God; a knowledgeable person without piety is a fruitless tree and fuel for Hell, while an ignorant worshipper lacks full God-consciousness.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r5.anchor: نقول التقوى ثمرة العلم قال الله تعالى : { إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء }

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r6.claim: The address does not imply that unbelievers retain equal honor: all created people initially acknowledged their Lord, but persistence increases their honor and turning away removes its trace.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r6.anchor: نقول ذلك غير لازم مع أنه حاصل بدليل قوله تعالى : { ولقد كرمنا بنىءادم } ( الإسراء : 70 ) لأن كل من خلق فقد اعترف بربه

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r7.claim: The minimum piety is to fulfill commands and avoid prohibitions without feeling secure or complacent; after a sin one should follow it with good, regret, and repentance rather than rely on time.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r7.anchor: أدنى مراتب التقوى أن يجتنب العبد المناهي ويأتي بالأوامر

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r8.claim: The most pious obeys and abstains while fearing God and attending only to Him; even a moment's turn toward self or child is counted as a fault at this highest rank.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r8.anchor: أما الأتقى فهو الذي يأتي بما أمر به ويترك ما نهى عنه ، وهو مع ذلك خاش ربه لا يشتغل بغير الله

RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r9.claim: Those at the lower rank are saved, while the highest are brought to the Garden; Rāzī likens the difference to a king's gardener versus a person kept close to the king and granted daily access to estates.
RAZI-FULL:v28p119#2/r9.anchor: وللأولين النجاة لقوله تعالى : { ثم ننجى الذين اتقوا } ( مريم : 72 ) وللآخرين السوق إلى الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v28p120/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p120/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p120/r1.claim: God knows outward appearances and lineages as well as inner secrets, so people should make piety their work and increase it as He increases them.
RAZI-FULL:v28p120/r1.anchor: أي عليم بظواهركم ، يعلم أنسابكم خبير ببواطنكم لا تخفى عليه أسراركم

STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r2.speaker: a minority
STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r2.claim: A minority considers verse 13 to be Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r2.anchor: a minority maintain that v. 13 is from the Makkan period (Āl)

STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r10.claim: The final section clarifies faith and belief, highlighting the Quran’s celebrated teaching that the most noble before God are the most reverent.
STUDYQURAN:49:intro/r10.anchor: The last part of this sūrah (vv. 13–18) clarifies the true nature of faith and belief

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r1.claim: The phrase may refer to Adam and Eve.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r1.anchor: From a male and a female can be understood as a reference to Adam and Eve (Q)

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r2.claim: Alternatively, it refers to each human being's creation from the fluids of a man and a woman.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r2.anchor: but also to the creation of each human being from the fluid of a man and a woman (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r3.claim: Differences in tribe, race, ethnicity, language, nationality, and religion can help people appreciate the reality of the human condition.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r3.anchor: That people have been divided into diverse peoples and tribes that they may come to know one another indicates the manner

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r4.claim: A hadith says God judges people by their hearts, not by their bodies or outward forms.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r4.anchor: In this regard, the Prophet has said, “God does not look at your bodies, nor at your forms. He looks at your hearts.”

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r5.speaker: ḥadīth
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r5.claim: A cited hadith presents the heart as determining the whole body's state: purity of heart purifies the body, while pollution corrupts it.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r5.anchor: In another ḥadīth, the heart is presented as the reality that determines all other dimensions of one’s being

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r6.claim: Human diversity is among the greatest worldly tests; 5:48 says God made people diverse to test them and directs them to compete in good deeds before returning to Him.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r6.anchor: as in 5:48: And had God willed, He would have made you one community

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r7.claim: Taqwā means reverence, God-fearing, or simply fearing in pre-Islamic usage.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r7.anchor: has the sense of “God-fearing,” or just “fearing” in pre-Islamic Arabia

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r8.claim: This late Madinan verse recasts Arabia's moral order: true worth rests on faith and piety rather than lineage or displays of valor and generosity, once treated as opposites to reverence.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r8.anchor: This late Madinan verse thus signals a revamping of the moral order of Arabia to one in which true worth is no longer determined by lineage

STUDYQURAN:49:13/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r9.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r9.claim: The Prophet reportedly said Islam removed jāhiliyyah zealotry and boasting of descent: all people descend from Adam, and the most beloved to God at Resurrection are the most obedient and reverent.
STUDYQURAN:49:13/r9.anchor: In this vein, the Prophet is reported to have said, “Truly God has ennobled those who were lowly during the Age of Ignorance.

TAB-FULL:v21p382/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p382/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p382/r1.claim: Human beings are created from the fluid of a male and the fluid of a female.
TAB-FULL:v21p382/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: " خلق الله الولد من ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، وقد قال تبارك وتعالى {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى} [الحجرات: 13] "

TAB-FULL:v21p382/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p382/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p382/r2.claim: Mujahid says a child is created from the fluids of both man and woman, citing this verse.
TAB-FULL:v21p382/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: " خلق الله الولد من ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، وقد قال تبارك وتعالى {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى} [الحجرات: 13] "

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r1.claim: Shuʿūb are broad lineages such as Mudar or Rabiʿa; tribes are nearer lineages such as Tamim or Bakr, with still closer subdivisions such as Shayban and Darim. Ibn al-Aḥmar’s verse attests the usage.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r1.anchor: وأقرب القبائل الأفخاذ وهما كشيبان من بكر ودارم من تميم، ونحو ذلك، ومن الشعب قول ابن أحمر الباهلي

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to gloss shuʿūb as groups and qabaʾil as clans or subdivisions.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} [الحجرات: 13] قال: " الشعوب: الجماع، والقبائل: البطون "

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r3.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash describes qabaʾil as major tribes, such as Banu Tamim, and as smaller subdivisions.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r3.anchor: قال خلاد: قال أبو بكر: " القبائل العظام، مثل بني تميم، والقبائل: الأفخاذ "

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr is reported to define shuʿūb as the broader population and qabaʾil as subdivisions.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r4.anchor: عن أبي حصين، عن سعيد بن جبير، {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} [الحجرات: 13] قال: " الشعوب: الجمهور، والقبائل: الأفخاذ "

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r5.claim: Mujahid defines shuʿūb as distant ancestry and qabaʾil as nearer lineage.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {شعوبا} [الحجرات: 13] قال: «النسب البعيد» {وقبائل} [الحجرات: 13] «دون ذلك»

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r6.claim: Qatadah likewise calls shuʿūb distant ancestry and says tribes are identified through nearer descent, such as being from a named clan.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {وجعلناكم شعوبا} [الحجرات: 13] قال: «هو النسب البعيد»

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says shuʿūb refer to distant ancestry.
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r7.anchor: حدثت عن الحسين قال: سمعت أبا معاذ، يقول: أخبرنا عبيد قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {وجعلناكم شعوبا} [الحجرات: 13] قال: " أما الشعوب: فالنسب البعيد "

TAB-FULL:v21p384/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v21p384/r8.claim: An unnamed view says shuʿūb are subdivisions of clans (afkhādh).

TAB-FULL:v21p385/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr is reported here to call shuʿūb subdivisions and qabaʾil tribes.
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r1.anchor: عن أبي حصين، عن سعيد بن جبير، {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} [الحجرات: 13] قال:

TAB-FULL:v21p385/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r2.claim: Another view makes shuʿūb clans and qabaʾil smaller subdivisions.
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: الشعوب: البطون، والقبائل: الأفخاذ

TAB-FULL:v21p385/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to define shuʿūb as clans and qabaʾil as the larger subdivisions.
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} [الحجرات: 13] قال:

TAB-FULL:v21p385/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r4.claim: Another view defines shuʿūb as lineages.

TAB-FULL:v21p385/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to define shuʿūb as lineages.
TAB-FULL:v21p385/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} [الحجرات: 13] قال: " الشعوب: الأنساب "

TAB-FULL:v21p386/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p386/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p386/r1.claim: People were divided into lineages so they could recognize one another’s kinship and relative distance; ancestry itself confers no virtue or closeness to God, for honor is through piety.
TAB-FULL:v21p386/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وقبائل لتعارفوا} [الحجرات: 13] قال: «جعلنا هذا لتعارفوا، فلان بن فلان

TAB-FULL:v21p386/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p386/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v21p386/r2.claim: Mujahid explains recognition as identifying someone’s lineage, for example by saying who belongs to which family.
TAB-FULL:v21p386/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وقبائل لتعارفوا} [الحجرات: 13] قال: «جعلنا هذا لتعارفوا، فلان بن فلان

TAB-FULL:v21p387/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r1.claim: The most honored before God are those who fulfill His duties and avoid His prohibitions, not those with the grandest household or largest clan.
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r1.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الناس لآدم وحواء كطف الصاع لم يملأوه، إن الله لا يسألكم عن أحسابكم ولا عن أنسابكم يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v21p387/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r2.claim: The Prophet says all people descend from Adam and Eve, God will not ask about pedigree at Judgment, and the most honored is the most pious.
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r2.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الناس لآدم وحواء كطف الصاع لم يملأوه، إن الله لا يسألكم عن أحسابكم ولا عن أنسابكم يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v21p387/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r3.claim: The Prophet says lineage gives no one precedence; only religion or righteous deeds confer merit, while foul speech, stinginess, and cowardice are sufficient disgrace.
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r3.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن أنسابكم هذه ليست بمساب على أحد، وإنما أنتم ولد آدم طف الصاع لم تملأوه

TAB-FULL:v21p387/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says people deny three verses, including this one, since they claim the most honored are those with the greatest household; he forgot the third verse.
TAB-FULL:v21p387/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " ثلاث آيات جحدهن الناس: الإذن كله "، وقال: {إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم}

TAB-FULL:v21p388/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p388/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p388/r1.claim: The most honored among people before God are those most mindful of Him through fulfilling obligations and avoiding sins, not those with greater ancestry or numbers.
TAB-FULL:v21p388/r1.anchor: إن الله أيها الناس ذو علم بأتقاكم عند الله وأكرمكم عنده، ذو خبرة بكم وبمصالحكم

TAB-FULL:v21p388/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p388/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p388/r2.claim: God knows who is most pious and honored and understands people, their interests, and all their affairs; nothing is hidden from Him.
TAB-FULL:v21p388/r2.anchor: إن الله أيها الناس ذو علم بأتقاكم عند الله وأكرمكم عنده، ذو خبرة بكم وبمصالحكم

BURSEVI:v9p73/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r1.claim: A shaʿb is a large group descending from one origin and comprises tribes; tribes comprise clans, then subclans, branches, and families, with no social grouping below the family.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r1.anchor: والشعب بفتح الشين الجمع العظيم المنتسبون إلى أصل واحد وهو يجمع القبائل والقبيلة تجمع العمائر

BURSEVI:v9p73/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r2.claim: An alternative classification calls non-Arab subdivisions shuʿub, Arab subdivisions qabaʾil, Israelite clans asbat, Qahtan shuʿub, and Adnan qabaʾil.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r2.anchor: وقيل الشعوب بطون العجم والقبائل بطون العرب والأسباط من بني إسرائيل

BURSEVI:v9p73/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r3.claim: لتعارفوا contracts لتتعارفوا by dropping one of the two tāʾs.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r3.anchor: أصله لتتعارفوا حذفت إحدى التاءين أي ليعرف بعضكم بعضا

BURSEVI:v9p73/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r4.claim: Tribes and family lines let people identify one another, not boast, claim superiority, or deny their fathers.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r4.anchor: أي ليعرف بعضكم بعضا بحسب الإنسان فلا يعتزي أحد إلى غير آبائه

BURSEVI:v9p73/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p73/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi explains that shared names are distinguished by tribal affiliation, as Zayd Tamimi from Zayd Qurashi.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r5.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : يعني دوكس كه بنام منتحد باشن بقيله متميز ميشوند نانه زيد تميمي از زيد قرشي

BURSEVI:v9p73/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r6.claim: Piety, not ancestry, determines honor before God, even for an Abyssinian black slave such as Bilal; if people compete, let it be in piety and divine grace.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r6.anchor: إن الأكرم عنده تعالى هو الأتقى وإن كان عبدا حبشيا أسود مثل بلال

BURSEVI:v9p73/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r7.claim: Bursevi reads the Prophet’s ‘I am master of Adam’s children, no boast’ as locating honor in servanthood rather than rank or messengership; calling Muhammad God’s servant before His messenger likewise honors him.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r7.anchor: إلى قوله عليه السلام : "أنا سيد ولد آدم ولا فخر" أي ليس الفخر ليس بالسيادة والرسالة بل العبودية

BURSEVI:v9p73/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r8.claim: A report tells of a black youth bought on condition he could pray all five prayers behind the Prophet; after illness and death, the Prophet visited and tended his washing and burial, deeply affecting the Emigrants and Helpers, and the verse was revealed.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r8.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله عليه السلام مر في سوق المدينة فرأى غلاما أسود يقول : من اشتراني

BURSEVI:v9p73/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r9.claim: God knows people and their deeds and is aware of their inward states.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r9.anchor: {إن الله عليم} بكم وبأعمالكم {خبير} ببواطن أحوالكم

BURSEVI:v9p73/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r10.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v9p73/r10.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh notes lineage has customary and legal relevance, such as a noblewoman not marrying a Nabati, but it yields to the greater worth of faith and piety.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r10.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في حواشيه والنسب وإن كان معتبرا عرفا وشرعا حتى لا تتزوج الشريفة بالنبطي

BURSEVI:v9p73/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p73/r11.claim: Lineage was selected as the strongest worldly boast because it is lasting and unearned; all lesser boasts, such as wealth, children, and gardens, are invalidated a fortiori because fortunes can change.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r11.anchor: والأمور التي يفتخر بها في الدنيا وإن كانت كثيرة لكن النسب أعلاها من حيث أنه ثابت مستمر

BURSEVI:v9p73/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r12.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v9p73/r12.claim: A hadith says all share one Lord and father, and no Arab, non-Arab, red, or black person excels another except through piety.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r12.anchor: وفي الحديث أن ربكم واحد وأبوكم واحد لا فضل لعربي على عجمي ولا لعجمي على عربي

BURSEVI:v9p73/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p73/r13.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v9p73/r13.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says scholars agree that distinction among people is only by piety.
BURSEVI:v9p73/r13.anchor: وعلى هذا إجماع العلماء كما في بحر العلوم هركرا تقوى بيشتر قدم أودر مرتبه فضل يشتر

TABATABAI:49:13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13/r1.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines a shaʿb as a large human community such as Rabia or Mudar, and a tribe as a subdivision such as Tamim within Mudar.
TABATABAI:49:13/r1.anchor: الشعوب جمع شعب بالكسر فالسكون وهو على ما في المجمع

TABATABAI:49:13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13/r2.claim: A tribe is a division below a people, such as Tamim within Mudar.
TABATABAI:49:13/r2.anchor: والقبائل جمع قبيلة وهي دون الشعب كتميم من مضر

TABATABAI:49:13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:49:13/r3.claim: Another view reverses the hierarchy: peoples are below tribes and are named for branching.
TABATABAI:49:13/r3.anchor: وقيل الشعوب دون القبائل وسميت بها لتشعبها

TABATABAI:49:13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:49:13/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines a shaʿb as a tribe branching from one community and explains the root through a valley's gathering and dispersal, so the verb can mean unite or divide.
TABATABAI:49:13/r4.anchor: قال الراغب الشعب القبيلة المنشعبة من حي واحد

TABATABAI:49:13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:49:13/r5.claim: A further gloss identifies peoples with non-Arabs and tribes with Arabs; the author says this seems reducible to one of the preceding definitions.

TABATABAI:49:13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r6.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:49:13/r6.claim: Commentators read male and female as Adam and Eve: all people share the same parents irrespective of color or ethnicity.
TABATABAI:49:13/r6.anchor: ذكر المفسرون أن الآية مسوقة لنفي التفاخر بالأنساب

TABATABAI:49:13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r7.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:49:13/r7.claim: On that reading, peoples and tribes exist for mutual recognition and the social ties and dealings that sustain community, not for lineage-based boasting.
TABATABAI:49:13/r7.anchor: لا لكرامة لبعضكم على بعض بل لأن تتعارفوا فيعرف بعضكم بعضا

TABATABAI:49:13/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:49:13/r8.claim: An alternative reads male and female generally and treats the verse as abolishing every class distinction, since everyone is born from a man and a woman.
TABATABAI:49:13/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد بالذكر والأنثى مطلق الرجل والمرأة

TABATABAI:49:13/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:49:13/r9.claim: On the broader reading, divinely created differences among peoples and tribes serve recognition and social cohesion, not superiority or virtue.

TABATABAI:49:13/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13/r10.claim: An objection says recognition does not clearly follow from abolishing all class distinctions, since the verse specifically condemns lineage pride.
TABATABAI:49:13/r10.anchor: واعترض عليه بأن الآية مسوقة لنفي التفاخر بالأنساب وذمه

TABATABAI:49:13/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13/r11.claim: The author answers that lineage is one form of class distinction: pride can be rejected because all share Adam and Eve, or because everyone is born from two people.
TABATABAI:49:13/r11.anchor: يمكن أن يناقش فيه أن الاختلاف في الأنساب من مصاديق الاختلاف الطبقاتي

TABATABAI:49:13/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13/r12.claim: If the clause clearly condemns lineage pride, the Adam-and-Eve reading is stronger; otherwise the broader reading is preferable for its inclusive scope.
TABATABAI:49:13/r12.anchor: إن كان ظاهرا في ذم التفاخر بالأنساب فأول الوجهين أوجه

TABATABAI:49:13/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13/r13.claim: This clause explains honor with God: human differences exist for recognition and cooperation, not boasting, enslavement, exploitation, group arrogance, or corruption that destroys life.
TABATABAI:49:13/r13.anchor: استئناف مبين لما فيه الكرامة عند الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r1.claim: People naturally seek distinction, but those attached to worldly life treat wealth, beauty, lineage, and status as honor and pursue them to boast over others.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r1.anchor: الإنسان مجبول على طلب ما يتميز به من غيره ويختص به من بين أقرانه

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r2.claim: These material distinctions are illusory and bring no real honor; instead they lead to ruin and misery.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r2.anchor: وهذه مزايا وهمية لا تجلب لهم شيئا من الشرف والكرامة

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r3.claim: Real honor leads to true happiness, eternal good life near God; taqwa is the sole means to afterlife happiness, followed by worldly happiness.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r3.anchor: والشرف الحقيقي هو الذي يؤدي الإنسان إلى سعادته الحقيقية وهو الحياة الطيبة الأبدية

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r4.claim: The author supports this with 8:67, where God wills the hereafter, and 2:197, which calls taqwa the best provision.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r4.anchor: تريدون عرض الدنيا والله يريد الآخرة

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r5.claim: God's chosen goal of taqwa creates no competition among its adherents, unlike imagined worldly goals such as wealth, leadership, beauty, fame, and ancestry.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r5.anchor: وهذه البغية والغاية التي اختارها الله بعلمه غاية للناس لا تزاحم فيها

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r6.claim: God's knowledge and awareness reinforce the verse: He chose real honor knowingly, while humanly chosen worldly adornments are false and imaginary.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r6.anchor: فيه تأكيد لمضمون الآية وتلويح إلى أن الذي اختاره الله كرامة للناس كرامة حقيقية

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r7.claim: The contrast between worldly adornment and the real afterlife also appears in 29:64.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r7.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان

TABATABAI:49:13-14/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r8.claim: The verse obliges people to pursue the ends their Lord commands and choose taqwa, the goal He selected and guides them toward.
TABATABAI:49:13-14/r8.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن من الواجب على الناس أن يتبعوا في غايات الحياة أمر ربهم

TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r5.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses peoples as non-Arabs and tribes as Arabs; al-Majmaʿ attributes the same report to al-Sadiq.
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r5.anchor: ونسبه في مجمع البيان إلى الصادق عليه السلام

TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r6.claim: In a Farewell address during the Days of Tashriq, the Prophet says all share one Lord and father and no Arab, non-Arab, or color group has precedence except through taqwa; witnesses should inform the absent.
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r7.claim: Al-Kafi reports that the Prophet married Miqdad ibn al-Aswad to Dubāʿa bint al-Zubayr to lower marriage barriers, model the practice, and show nobility rests on taqwa.
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r7.anchor: عن أبي بكر الحضرمي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن رسول الله

TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r8.claim: Asked what nobility is, Abu Abd Allah answers: taqwa.
TABATABAI:49:11-18#3/r8.anchor: عن جميل بن دراج قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام فما الكرم

TABRISI:49:13/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:49:13/r6.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about Thābit ibn Qays: after he insulted a man who did not make room, the Prophet asked him to look at the people; Thābit saw differing skin colors, and the Prophet said superiority is only through piety and religion.
TABRISI:49:13/r6.anchor: قيل نزلت في ثابت بن قيس بن شماس

TABRISI:49:11-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:11-14/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:49:11-14/r1.claim: The preceding account about Thābit ibn Qays and the man he insulted is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās.

TABRISI:49:11-14/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:11-14/r2.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:49:11-14/r2.claim: Muqātil reports that at the conquest of Mecca, men objected to Bilāl's call to prayer from the Kaaba because of his color and lineage; Gabriel informed the Prophet, who confronted them, and the verse rebuked them.
TABRISI:49:11-14/r2.anchor: وزجرهم عن التفاخر بالأنساب والازدراء بالفقر والتكاثر بالأموال عن مقاتل

TABRISI:49:11-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:11-14/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:49:11-14/r3.claim: The verse follows the command to reconcile people by forbidding mockery, contempt for the poor, and other causes of division.
TABRISI:49:11-14/r3.anchor: لما أمر سبحانه بإصلاح ذات البين ونهى عن التفرق عقب ذلك بالنهي عن أسباب الفرقة

TABRISI:49:13#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:49:13#2/r13.claim: “A male and a female” means Adam and Eve; all people are equal in lineage because everyone descends from them, so God forbids boasting about ancestry.
TABRISI:49:13#2/r13.anchor: أي من آدم وحواء والمعنى أنكم متساوون في النسب

TABRISI:49:13#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:49:13#3/r1.claim: All people descend from a man and a woman; superiority comes only through piety.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r1.anchor: إنما أنتم من رجل وامرأة كجمام الصاع ليس لأحد على أحد فضل إلا بالتقوى

TABRISI:49:13#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:49:13#3/r2.claim: Shuʿūb are large tribal groups such as Mudar and Rabiʿa; qabāʾil are subdivisions such as Bakr and Tamim.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r2.anchor: وهي جمع شعب وهو الحي العظيم مثل مضر وربيعة وقبائل هي دون الشعوب

TABRISI:49:13#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:49:13#3/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reverses the hierarchy: shuʿūb are below qabāʾil because they branch and divide from them.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r3.anchor: الشعوب دون القبائل وإنما سميت بذلك لتشعبها وتفرقها عن الحسن

TABRISI:49:13#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
TABRISI:49:13#3/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through ʿAtaʾ identifies shuʿūb as clients and qabāʾil as Arabs.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r4.anchor: أراد بالشعوب الموالي وبالقبائل العرب في رواية عطاء عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:49:13#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r5.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:49:13#3/r5.claim: Another classification makes shuʿūb non-Arabs, qabāʾil Arabs, and asbāṭ the Children of Israel; it is also reported from al-Sadiq.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r5.anchor: الشعوب من العجم والقبائل من العرب والأسباط من بني إسرائيل وروي ذلك عن الصادق

TABRISI:49:13#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:49:13#3/r6.claim: Lineages let people recognize one another by ancestry, father, and community; otherwise transactions fail and hadith cannot be transmitted.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r6.anchor: فيعرف بعضكم بعضا بنسبه وأبيه وقومه ولولا ذلك لفسدت المعاملات وخربت الدنيا

TABRISI:49:13#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:49:13#3/r7.claim: The most honored has the greatest reward and highest standing by avoiding sins and obeying God most fully.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r7.anchor: أكثركم ثوابا وأرفعكم منزلة عند الله أتقاكم لمعاصيه وأعملكم بطاعته

TABRISI:49:13#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:49:13#3/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says people neglected God's command and exalted lineages, so God will elevate His own lineage, lower theirs, and call for the pious.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r8.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:49:13#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:49:13#3/r9.claim: Asked who is best, Jesus takes two handfuls of earth: people come from earth, and the most pious is most honorable.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r9.anchor: وروي أن رجلا سأل عيسى ابن مريم أي الناس أفضل فأخذ قبضتين من تراب

TABRISI:49:13#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:49:13#3/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet tracing his placement through the best group, third, tribe, and house, citing Qur'anic divisions and the purification of his family.
TABRISI:49:13#3/r10.anchor: عن عباية ابن ربعى عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TABRISI:49:13-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:49:13-14/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:49:13-14/r1.claim: God knows people's deeds and is fully aware of their circumstances; nothing is hidden from Him.
TABRISI:49:13-14/r1.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء من ذلك

THALABI:v9p86/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p86/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p86/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse followed Thabit ibn Qays calling a man son of so-and-so for not making room; the Prophet told Thabit that only religion and piety give precedence, and linked the episode to the instruction to make room in gatherings.
THALABI:v9p86/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس وقوله للرجل الذي لم يفسح له: ابن فلانة،

THALABI:v9p86/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p86/r2.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v9p86/r2.claim: Muqatil says the verse followed Bilal's call to prayer from the Kaaba roof at the conquest: Attab, al-Harith, and Suhayl made racial remarks, while Abu Sufyan feared revelation; after they confessed, the Prophet received the verse.
THALABI:v9p86/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لما كان يوم فتح مكة، أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا حتى علا على ظهر الكعبة وأذن،

THALABI:v9p86/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p86/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p86/r3.claim: The verse rebukes boasting in ancestry or wealth and looking down on poor people; honor before God rests on piety.
THALABI:v9p86/r3.anchor: فأنزل الله سبحانه هذه الآية وزجرهم، عن التفاخر بالأنساب، والتكاثر بالأموال، والازدراء للفقراء

THALABI:v9p87/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r1.speaker: يزيد بن سخرة
THALABI:v9p87/r1.claim: Yazid reports that a Black enslaved boy stipulated that he be allowed to pray the five daily prayers behind the Prophet; after the boy died, the Prophet washed and buried him, and the revelation showed that piety outranks status.
THALABI:v9p87/r1.anchor: وقال يزيد بن سخرة: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم يمر ببعض أسواق المدينة، فإذا غلام أسود قائم،

THALABI:v9p87/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p87/r2.claim: The shuʿūb are the leading, broad groupings of tribes, including Rabiʿa, Mudar, Aws, and Khazraj.
THALABI:v9p87/r2.anchor: وهي رؤوس القبائل وجمهورها مثل ربيعة ومضر والأوس والخزرج.

THALABI:v9p87/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p87/r3.claim: Shuʿūb is singular shaʿb; the name evokes branching and gathering, like the branches of a tree.
THALABI:v9p87/r3.anchor: واحدها شعب بفتح الشين، سموا بذلك لتشعبهم واجتماعهم، كتشعب أغصان الشجر،

THALABI:v9p87/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p87/r4.claim: The root can mean either gathering or separating, and death is consequently called Shuʿūb.
THALABI:v9p87/r4.anchor: والشعب من الأضداد يقال: شعبته إذا جمعته، وشعبته إذا فرقته، ومنه قيل للموت: شعوب.

THALABI:v9p87/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p87/r5.claim: The social hierarchy descends from tribes to clans, lineages, branches, and families; examples include Kinda, Tamim, Shayban, Darim, Banu Ghalib, Banu Luʾayy, Banu Hashim, and Umayya.
THALABI:v9p87/r5.anchor: وقبائل وهي دون الشعوب، واحدها قبيلة، وهم كندة من ربيعة، وتميم من مضر، ودون القبائل العمائر،

THALABI:v9p87/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v9p87/r6.claim: One reported classification takes the peoples as non-Arabs, the tribes as Arabs, and the asbat as the tribes of Israel.
THALABI:v9p87/r6.anchor: وقيل: الشعوب من العجم، والقبائل من العرب، والأسباط من بني إسرائيل،

THALABI:v9p87/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p87/r7.speaker: أبو رزين وأبو روق
THALABI:v9p87/r7.claim: Abu Razin and Abu Rawq say peoples are those affiliated with cities, villages, and lands, while Arab tribes are affiliated with their fathers.
THALABI:v9p87/r7.anchor: وقال أبو رزين وأبو روق: الشعوب الذين لا يصيرون إلى أحد، بل ينسبون إلى المدائن، والقرى،

THALABI:v9p88/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p88/r1.claim: The purpose is mutual recognition of close and distant kinship, not boasting about ancestry.
THALABI:v9p88/r1.anchor: لتعارفوا يعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب النسب، وبعده لا لتفاخروا.

THALABI:v9p88/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r2.speaker: الأعمش وابن عباس
THALABI:v9p88/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads l-yataʿārafū, adding a ta; Ibn ʿAbbas reads li-yaʿrifū, without the alif.
THALABI:v9p88/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش (ليتعارفوا) ، وقرأ ابن عباس (ليعرفوا) بغير (ألف)

THALABI:v9p88/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r3.speaker: العامة
THALABI:v9p88/r3.claim: The open hamza connects the clause to what precedes; the majority read with kasra as a new sentence and pause after li-taʿārafū.
THALABI:v9p88/r3.anchor: إن أكرمكم بفتح (الألف) ، وقرأه العامة (إن) بكسر (الألف) على الاستئناف، والوقوف على قوله لتعارفوا

THALABI:v9p88/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v9p88/r4.claim: Qatada says piety is the highest nobility and wickedness the basest disgrace.
THALABI:v9p88/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: في هذه الآية أكرم الكرم التقوى. وألأم اللوم الفجور،

THALABI:v9p88/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p88/r5.claim: The Prophet says whoever wishes to be the noblest of people should fear God.
THALABI:v9p88/r5.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من سره أن يكون أكرم الناس، فليتق الله»

THALABI:v9p88/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p88/r6.claim: A prophetic saying defines a man's nobility by religion and piety, his origin by intelligence, and his standing by character.
THALABI:v9p88/r6.anchor: وقال: «كرم الرجل دينه، وتقواه، وأصله عقله، وحسبه خلقه»

THALABI:v9p88/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p88/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas distinguishes worldly nobility, which is wealth, from the nobility of the afterlife, which is piety.
THALABI:v9p88/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كرم الدنيا الغنى، وكرم الآخرة التقوى:

THALABI:v9p88/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p88/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's conquest-day sermon: he abolished pre-Islamic pride in ancestry, divided people into the pious and wicked, and recited this verse.
THALABI:v9p88/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: طاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على راحلته القصواء يوم الفتح يستلم الركن بمحجنه، فما وجد لها مناخ

THALABI:v9p88/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p88/r9.claim: The Prophet says God regards people's hearts and deeds rather than their appearances and wealth, and that the most Godfearing are the noblest of Adam's children.
THALABI:v9p88/r9.anchor: إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم، ولا إلى أموالكم، ولكن ينظر إلى قلوبكم، وأعمالكم،

THALABI:v9p88#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88#2/r1.speaker: الله سبحانه
THALABI:v9p88#2/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God's declaration that He set piety as the true lineage and will raise the pious while lowering the genealogies people boast about.
THALABI:v9p88#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: الله سبحانه يقول يوم القيامة: إني جعلت نسبا، وجعلتم نسبا،

THALABI:v9p88#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v9p88#2/r2.claim: When asked who the noblest person is, the Prophet answers: the most pious.
THALABI:v9p88#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قيل: يا رسول الله من أكرم الناس؟ قال: «أتقاهم»

THALABI:v9p88#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p88#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الفرحان
THALABI:v9p88#2/r3.claim: Umar ibn al-Farhan's poem contrasts wealth's prestige with the true glory of the pious and says that knowledge of God that does not benefit its possessor leaves him wretched.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r1.claim: The verse rebukes boasting about lineage or wealth and looking down on the poor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r1.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الزجر عن التفاخر بالأنساب والتكاثر بالأموال والازدراء بالفقراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Abu Salih as reported by al-Kalbi, says the verse followed Thabit ibn Qays insulting a man by recalling the woman's lineage he had mocked; the Prophet had Thabit look at the gathered people and said superiority is only through religion and piety.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r2.anchor: على ما ذكره الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس: أن ثابت بن قيس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed when four Quraysh men mocked Bilal's blackness after Muhammad ordered him to call the adhan atop the Kaaba at the conquest of Mecca.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في بلال المؤذن وفي أربعة نفر من قريش عابوه بسواده يوم فتح مكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r4.claim: People are Adam's and Eve's descendants and equal in lineage, so no one is superior to another by ancestry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r4.anchor: يعني: آدم وحواء، والمعنى: أنكم متساوون في النسب، ليس يفضل أحد غيره بنسبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said that everyone is a child of Adam and descends from one man, like the small measure of a ṣāʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r5.anchor: كما قال رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء وأهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda, al-Farra, and language scholars say a shaʿb is larger than a tribe, like Mudar or Rabi'a; tribes within them include Bakr of Rabi'a and Tamim of Mudar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p362#2/r6.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة (¬2) والفراء (¬3) وجميع أهل اللغة (¬4) قالوا: الشعب أعظم من القبيلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r1.claim: The purpose of peoples' divisions is to recognize one another by nearer and more distant degrees of kinship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r1.anchor: أي: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب النسب وبعده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r2.claim: Muqatil says the verse identifies Bilal as the most pious and honored.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني: بلالا (¬6) أخبر أن أتقاهم بلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that God will say on Judgment Day that people rejected the Godfearing rank He assigned, insisting on human pedigrees instead; God will raise His own lineage and lower theirs, then call for the pious.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r3.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r4.speaker: أهل العلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r4.claim: The scholars say the verse forbids despising, humiliating, or asserting superiority over people because of lineage or ancestors.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r4.anchor: وقال أهل العلم: هذا في الزجر عن الازدراء بالناس والتحقير لهم لأجل النسب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r5.claim: Lineage is nevertheless considered in marriage compatibility by consensus, based on connection to the Prophet's lineage or inherited knowledge from him; a report says every cause and lineage ends at Judgment Day except his.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r5.anchor: فأما اعتبار النسب في الكفاءة فإن ذلك متفق عليه، والأصل فيه شيئان: نسب يتصل برسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r6.claim: The ancestry of rulers, ministers, leaders, or oppressors is not a condition of marriage compatibility; piety is required, as is the foundation of religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p366/r6.anchor: فأما نسب الأمراء والوزراء والرؤساء والظلمة، فذلك مما لا يشترط في الكفاءة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r5.claim: All people descend from the same father and mother, so lineage gives no basis for superiority.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r5.anchor: أي: كلكم بنو أب واحد وأم واحدة، فلا تفاضل بينكم في النسب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r6.claim: Shuʿub are the heads of tribes, such as Rabi'a and Mudar; tribes are subdivisions, such as Bakr of Rabi'a and Tamim of Mudar.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r6.anchor: وهي رؤوس القبائل، كربيعة ومضر { وقبائل } وهي دون الشعوب كبكر من ربيعة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r7.claim: Peoples and tribes exist so people can recognize degrees of kinship, near and distant, not to boast about ancestry.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r7.anchor: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب النسب وبعده لا لتتفاخروا بها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r8.claim: The most honored person before God is the one most mindful of Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:49:12-13/r8.anchor: ثم أعلم أن أرفعهم عنده منزلة أتقاهم

QASHANI:49:13-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:49:13-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:49:13-14/r1.claim: Lineage brings no honor because all share human origin; peoples and tribes enable recognition, not boasting. Honor comes only by avoiding vices, which is the root of piety.
QASHANI:49:13-14/r1.anchor: لا كرامة بالنسب لتساوي الكل في البشرية المنتسبة إلى ذكر وأنثى والامتياز بالشعوب والقبائل إنما يكون لأجل التعارف بالانتساب لا للتفاخر

QASHANI:49:13-14/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:49:13-14/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:49:13-14/r2.claim: Piety ranks upward from avoiding legal sins to avoiding moral vices such as ignorance, miserliness, greed, avarice, and cowardice.
QASHANI:49:13-14/r2.anchor: المتقي عن المناهي الشرعية التي هي الذنوب في عرف ظاهر الشرع أكرم من الفاجر وعن الرذائل الخلقية كالجهل والبخل والشره والحرص والجبن

QASHANI:49:13-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:49:13-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:49:13-14/r3.claim: Beyond moral virtue is trust in God and witnessing God's acts rather than crediting effects to others; beyond this is seeing through acts to the manifestations of God's acts.
QASHANI:49:13-14/r3.anchor: ومشاهدة أفعال الحق أكرم من الفاضل المتدرب بالفضائل الخلقية المعتد بتأثير الغير، المحجوب برؤية أفعال الحق

QASHANI:49:13-14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:49:13-14/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:49:13-14/r4.claim: Higher still is release from attribute-veils through satisfaction and erasure of attributes, then annihilation of the particular selfhood that is the root of sins.
QASHANI:49:13-14/r4.anchor: المحجوب بالصفات عن تجليات صفات الحق وعن وجوده المخصوص

QASHANI:49:13-14/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:49:13-14/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:49:13-14/r5.claim: God knows the different ranks of people's piety and is aware of their relative degrees.
QASHANI:49:13-14/r5.anchor: { إن الله عليم } بمراتب تقواكم { خبير } بتفاضلكم

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r1.claim: Humanity was created either from Adam and Eve or, distributively, each person from a mother and father; all are equal in this respect, with no grounds for pride or tribal contempt.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r1.anchor: Âdem ile Havvâ’dan yahut her birinizi bir ana ile bir babadan yarattık, yani bu cihetle hepiniz müsâvîsiniz, birbirinize karşı övünmeye veya şu kavim bu kavim diye tahkir etmeye hak yoktur.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r2.claim: This common humanity creates a brotherhood that should prevent mockery and backbiting, likened to eating one another's flesh.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r2.anchor: etini yercesine gıybete mâni‘olmak lâzım gelir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r3.claim: Peoples and tribes exist so people may recognize one another by ancestry and cooperate, not boast in lineage.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r3.anchor: tanışasınız yani soylarınız, atalarınızla tefâhur için değil birbirinizi soyu sopu ile tanıyarak ona göre yardımlaşasınız.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r4.claim: Shuʿūb is the plural of shaʿb and qabāʾil the plural of qabīla; Arab social ranks were named by analogy with parts of the human head and body.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r4.anchor: “Şu‘ûb” “şa‘b”ın cem‘i, “kabâil” “kabîle”nin cem‘idir. Araplar, cemiyet taksîmâtını insan bedeninin hilkatini esas ittihaz ederek yapmışlardır.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r5.claim: In the bodily analogy, skull bones are qabīla and their joining suture is shaʿb; a shared-ancestor shaʿb includes tribes, then amāra, baṭn, faḫdh, and faṣīla, with some adding a seventh level, ʿashīra.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r5.anchor: İnsanın kafatasını teşkil eden baş kemiklerinden her birine “kabîle” ve mecmû‘una “kabâil” denir ve bu baş kemiklerinin birbirine kavuşup bitiştiği eke de “şa‘b” ıtlak edilir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r6.claim: His example maps Huzayma to shaʿb, Kināna to qabīla, Quraysh to amāra, Quṣayy to baṭn, Hāshim to faḫdh, and ʿAbbās to faṣīla.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r6.anchor: Huzeyme bir şa‘b, Kinâne bir kabile, Kureyş bir amâre, Kusay bir batn, Hâşim bir fahz, Abbas bir fasîledir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r7.speaker: müfessirîn
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r7.claim: Some exegetes instead take tribes to refer to Arab subdivisions and peoples to the subdivisions of non-Arab nations.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r7.anchor: “kabâil” Arap batınlarına, “şu‘ûb” da Acem, yani Arabın gayrı akvâm batınlarına işaret olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r8.claim: Division into peoples and tribes is for recognition, mutual help and affection, practicing good character, and forming larger, stronger communities for protection, not quarrelling, insulting, or fighting.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r8.anchor: tanışıp yardımlaşarak sevişmek ve güzel ahlâkları tatbik ederek daha büyük, daha güzel cemiyetler husûle getirip korunmak içindir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r9.claim: Taqwa is the whole basis of human spiritual excellence and rank before God; ancestry or belonging to a particular people is not the measure, and those seeking high rank must hold to taqwa.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r9.anchor: Nefislerin kemâlâtının ve şahısların merâtib ve derecâtının bütün medârı takvâdır. Şu, bu zâtın nesebinden veya fülân kavmin soyundan olmak değildir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r10.claim: Atqā is the elative form from taqwa; taqwa derives from wiqāya, intense guarding and preservation, with its root letters transformed to mean putting the soul under protection from feared things.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r10.anchor: “Etkā” “takvâ”dan ism-i tafdîldir. Yukarılarda da geçtiği üzere “takvâ” lügatta “vikāye”dendir. “Vikāye” fart-ı sıyânet, yani gayet iyi korunup sakınmaktır.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r11.claim: In language, taqwa can also be called fear, and fear taqwa.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r11.anchor: Sonra bazen korkuya takvâ ve takvâya korku tâbir olunur.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r12.claim: In its broad legal sense, taqwa means avoiding what harms one in the afterlife, on a scale from avoiding shirk to total purification and turning wholly to God; 3:102 describes true taqwa.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r12.anchor: Birisi geniş olan âm mânasıdır ki sonunda âhirette muzır olandan sakınıp korunmak demektir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r13.claim: In the conventional, unqualified legal sense, taqwa is guarding oneself against any act or omission that makes one liable to punishment; avoiding major sins is unanimously required, while avoiding minor sins is debated.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r13.anchor: Bir de şer‘de müte‘âref olan hâs mânası vardır ki mutlak olarak takvâ denildiği ve karîne bulunmadığı zaman murad bu olur: Nefsi ukūbete müstahik kılacak gerek fiil ve gerek terk herhangi bir günahtan korumaktır.

ELMALILI:49:13-18/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r14.claim: A hadith transmitted by Tirmidhī and others says one is not among the God-fearing until one leaves what is harmless to avoid what is harmful; the author infers avoiding doubtful lawful matters and prohibitively disliked acts.
ELMALILI:49:13-18/r14.anchor: Tirmizî ve sâirenin rivayet ettiği bir hadîs-i şerifte

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r1.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib defines taqwa in customary religious usage as guarding the soul from sin: leaving forbidden acts accomplishes this, and leaving permissible acts completes it, since doubtful boundaries can lead into the forbidden.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r1.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “Şer‘in te‘ârüfünde ‘takvâ’ nefsi ismden hıfzetmektir, bu ise haramı terk ile olur, bu da mubâhâtı terk ile tamam olur.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r2.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says lawful and forbidden matters are clear but doubtful matters are known to few; avoiding them protects religion and honor, while entering them risks the forbidden, like a shepherd at a preserve, and the heart governs the body's soundness.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r2.anchor: Buhârî, Müslim ve sâirede tahric olunduğu üzere Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki: “Helâl belli, haram da bellidir, yani şer‘an beyan olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r3.speaker: Birgivî
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r3.claim: Birgivī says linguistic taqwa remains operative in law and extreme caution entails avoiding minor sins and doubts; since avoiding every doubt is now impossible, avoid doubts near the forbidden, as duty is limited by capacity, including all forbidden and prohibitively disliked acts.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r3.anchor: Lügavî mâna şer‘de mümkin olduğu kadar mer‘îdir. Fart-ı sıyânet mânası ise sağāir ve şübühâttan dahi korunmayı iktizâ eder.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r4.claim: The preceding account implies that taqwa has three levels and requires knowledge of the sins and dangers to avoid; this points to the teaching that only the knowledgeable truly fear God.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r4.anchor: bunlar gösteriyor ki takvâlı olabilmek için korunulması lâzım gelen günahları, tehlikeleri bilmek lâzım gelecek

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r5.claim: If taqwa is understood through its necessary companion, awe and fear, “most God-fearing” also expresses “most fearful of God.”
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r5.anchor: Bu cihetle takvâ lâzımı olan havf ü haşyet ile tefsir edilecek olursa en takvâlı demek Allah’tan en çok korkan mânasını da ifade eder.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r6.claim: The rule that the most honored before God is the most God-fearing is a central aim of the sūra, echoed by its opening command to fear God and its description of hearts tested for taqwa.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r6.anchor: Başta وَاتَّقُوا اللهَّٰ ve أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱمْتَحَنَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ buyurulması da bunu anlatır.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r7.claim: An unnamed hadith says whoever is glad to be the most honored among people should be mindful of God.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r7.anchor: nâsın en mükerremi olmak mesrur ederse Allah’a takvâlı olsun

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r8.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says people are of two kinds: the faithful and God-fearing, honored by God, and the sinful and wretched, contemptible before God.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r8.anchor: diğer bir hadîs-i şerifte de Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm buyurmuştur: “Ey nâs! İnsanlar iki adamdan ibarettir: Biri mü’min, takī, Allah yanında kerîm; biri de fâcir, şakī, Allah yanında hakir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
