ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r9.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that worldly honor is wealth, whereas the honor of the afterlife is taqwa.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r9.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan da şöyle mervîdir: “Dünyanın keremi

ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r10.claim: God knows people and all they do and knows their inner states; He alone knows which of them is most God-fearing.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#2/r10.anchor: sizi ve her yaptığınızı bilir ve ahvâlinizin iç yüzünden de haberdardır. Hanginiz etkā olduğunu O bilir.

ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r1.claim: A third sense makes Islam higher than faith, a perfection including ihsan (2:112), the reality of 3:19, and the God-consciousness encouraged in 49:13.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r1.anchor: Üçüncüsü: İmandan ehas ve onun bir kemâli, bir gayesi olmak üzere fevkinde olan islâmdır

ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r17.claim: He identifies Sūrat Qāf as Meccan with forty-five verses.
ELMALILI:49:13-18#4/r17.anchor: سُورَةُ قۤ مَ ِّكي َّةٌ وَهِيَ خمَْسٌ وَأَرْبـَعُونَ اٰيَةً

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r1.claim: This verse is one foundation for the worldview and standards of value held by Muslims.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r1.anchor: Müslümanların dünya görüşlerini ve değer ölçütlerini dayandırdıkları âyetlerden biri de budur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r2.claim: Political, cultural, biological, and geographic differences distinguish people and groups, giving them identities through which they are recognized and meet one another; people also turn these differences into pride.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r2.anchor: Fertler, gruplar, kavimler, ümmetler, milletler siyasî, kültürel, biyolojik, coğrafî vb. farklarla birbirinden ayrılır; bu farklara bağlı olarak farklı kimlik sahibi olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r3.claim: The verse affirms the purpose of differing identities as recognition and acquaintance, while rejecting social or ethnic membership as a basis for superiority.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r3.anchor: Âyet farklı yaratılmanın “kimlik edinme ve bu kimlikle tanınma, tanışma” fonksiyon ve hikmetini onaylıyor; ancak farklı sosyal ve etnik gruplara mensup olmanın üstünlük vesilesi olarak kullanılmasını reddediyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r4.claim: A person's honor depends on universal values won through personal choice and effort, not ethnic affiliation that was not chosen.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r4.anchor: insanın şeref ve değerini, kendi iradesi ile elde etmediği etnik aidiyete değil, kendi irade ve çabasıyla elde ettiği evrensel değerlere bağlıyor.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r5.claim: Taqwā here means acquiring universal virtues and carefully avoiding their opposites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r5.anchor: Âyetteki etka kelimesinin içerdiği takvâ kavramı, evrensel değerleri, erdemleri edinme ve bunların zıtlarından titizlikle kaçınma ve sakınmayı ifade etmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r6.claim: Apart from faith in the true religion, whoever has universal values is superior in that respect; for eternal salvation, however, no other value or virtue can replace faith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r6.anchor: Hak dine iman dışındaki evrensel değerler hangi kişi ve grupta bulunursa o, diğerlerinden daha üstündür, daha değerlidir. Sıra hak dine imana gelince

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r7.claim: All humanity comes from Adam and Eve: Adam was made from earth, his wife from his own substance, and humanity then grew through their children; people share one origin and biological basis.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r7.anchor: Bütün insanlar bir erkekle (Âdem) bir kadından (Havvâ) yaratılmış, meydana getirilmiştir. Allah Âdem’i topraktan, eşini de Âdem’in aslından yaratmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r8.claim: People of common roots form groups for mutual recognition and solidarity; religion is the central bond, and those sharing a religion regard each other as siblings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r8.anchor: Kök itibariyle kardeş olan insanlar birçok hikmet yanında farklı kimliklerle tanınıp tanışmaları için gruplara ayrılmışlardır. Her grup, başkalarından farklı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r9.claim: Religion's most important value is moral character; morality should measure superiority both within a group and between groups.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r9.anchor: Dinin insana kazandırmak istediği en önemli değer ahlâktır (takvâ), hem bir grup içinde hem de gruplar arasında üstünlüğün, üstün değerin ölçütü ahlâk olmalıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r10.claim: Arabian tribal pride was strong; some noble families resisted marrying daughters to other clans or freedmen, and the Prophet opposed this and taught believers equality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r10.anchor: Kur’an’ın nâzil olduğu zamanda Araplar’da da kavimleri ve kabileleri ile övünme, kendilerini bu yüzden başkalarından üstün görme âdeti (kültürü) güçlü bir şekilde mevcuttu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r11.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r11.claim: In the Farewell Sermon, the Prophet said humanity has one Lord and father and that race, skin color, and Arab identity confer no superiority beyond piety and moral excellence; he asked hearers to pass this on.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:49:13/r11.anchor: Hz. Peygamber bunlarla mücadele etti, müminleri eğitti ve meşhur Vedâ hutbesinde bütün insanlığa şöyle seslendi: “Ey insanlar! Şunu iyi biliniz ki rabbiniz birdir, babanız birdir.

BAQILLANI:v1p132/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r1.speaker: محمد
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r1.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet rejected tribal pride and status by ancestry, reminding Quraysh that all people descend from Adam and reciting that piety is the measure of honor with God.
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r1.anchor: يا معشر قريش إن الله قد أذهب عنكم نخوة الجاهلية وتعظمها بالآباء

BAQILLANI:v1p132/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r2.speaker: محمد
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r2.claim: The Prophet declared former claims of vengeance, blood, or wealth void, except for custodianship of the Kaʿba and supplying water to pilgrims.
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r2.anchor: ألا كل مأثرة أو دم أو مال يدعى - فهو تحت قدمي هاتين إلا سدانة البيت وسقاية الحاج

BAQILLANI:v1p132/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r3.speaker: محمد
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r3.claim: For a death caused by a whip or stick in an assault short of intentional killing, he prescribed an aggravated blood-money of forty pregnant camels.
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r3.anchor: وقتيل الخطإ العمد بالسوط والعصا - فيه الدية مغلظة منها أربعون خلفة في بطونها أولادها

BAQILLANI:v1p132/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r4.speaker: محمد
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r4.claim: When the Prophet asked what he would do with Quraysh, they appealed to his generosity; he then released them, calling them free.
BAQILLANI:v1p132/r4.anchor: قالوا خيرا أخ كريم وابن أخ كريم ثم قال فاذهبوا فأنتم الطلقاء

QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r6.claim: All people descend from Adam and Eve and were divided into peoples and tribes for mutual recognition, not boasting or rivalry.
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r6.anchor: إنا خلقناكم أجمعكم من آدم وحواء ، ثم جعناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا لا لتكاثروا ولا لتنافسوا

QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r7.claim: There is no basis for pride in origins that reduce to earth, semen, or a clot, nor in what one's visible form conceals.
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r7.anchor: فإذا كانت الأصول تربة ونطفة وعلقة . . فالتفاخر بماذا ؟ أبا لحمأ المسنون ؟ أم بالنطفة في قرار مكين ؟

QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r8.claim: A saying that people's traces identify them urges the reader to look at their traces after they are gone.
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r8.anchor: وقد قيل : إن آثارنا تدل علينا . . . فانظروا بعدنا إلى الآثار

QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r9.claim: Ostentatious deeds, self-admiring states, and treacherous dealings cannot ground a claim to nobility.
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r9.anchor: أم بأفعالك التي هي بالرياء مشوبة ؟ أم بأحوالك التي هي بالإعجاب مصحوبة ؟ أم بمعاملاتك التي هي ملأى بالخيانة ؟

QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r10.claim: Piety means release from the self, its cravings, and its claims; the noblest servant is farthest from self and nearest to God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p222/r10.anchor: أتقاكم أي أبعدكم عن نفسه ، فالتقوى هي التحرر من النفس وأطماعها وحظوظها

BURHAN:v1p194#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r1.claim: In the listed chronology of Medinan revelations, Surat al-Hujurat comes after al-Mujadila and before al-Tahrim.
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r1.anchor: ثم المنافقون ثم المجادلة ثم الحجرات ثم ﴿ يا أيها النبي لم تحرم ﴾

BURHAN:v1p194#2/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r6.claim: The source gives totals of 85 Meccan and 29 Medinan surahs, while noting that reports differ.
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r6.anchor: فجميع ما نزل بمكة خمس وثمانون سورة وجميع ما نزل بالمدينة تسع وعشرون على اختلاف الروايات

BURHAN:v1p194#2/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r7.claim: Although 49:13 was revealed in Mecca on the day of its conquest, it is classified as Medinan because it came after the Hijra.
BURHAN:v1p194#2/r7.anchor: ونزولها بمكة يوم فتحها وهى مدنية لأنها نزلت بعد الهجرة

ITQAN:v1p62/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p62/r12.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
ITQAN:v1p62/r12.claim: Al-Wahidi reports from Ibn Abi Mulayka that this verse came down at the conquest of Mecca after Bilal called the prayer from the Kaaba and some objected to a Black enslaved man doing so.
ITQAN:v1p62/r12.anchor: أخرج الواحدي عن ابن أبي مليكة أنها نزلت بمكة يوم الفتح لما رقي بلال على ظهر الكعبة وأذن فقال بعض الناس

SULAMI:v2p263#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r1.claim: God made peoples and tribes for mutual recognition, not boasting over one another.
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم في هذه الآية : قال الله تعالى جعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا لا لتتفاخروا

SULAMI:v2p263#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r2.claim: Boasting about anything apart from religion, faith, Islam, or divinely granted spiritual ranks is boasting over nothing.
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم في هذه الآية : قال الله تعالى جعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا لا لتتفاخروا فمن افتخر

SULAMI:v2p263#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن محمد
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r3.claim: In an encounter with Abu Yaʿla al-ʿAlawi, ʿAbd Allah challenged pride in outward status by recalling the Prophet’s saying, “I am the lord of Adam’s children, without boasting.”
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r3.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن محمد يقول : دخل أبو يعلى العلوي على عبد الله فنظر إليه عبد الله وإلى ثيابه وزيه

SULAMI:v2p263#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r4.speaker: عبد الله المعلم
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r4.claim: His pride was not in being made lord of Adam’s children, but in the One who made him their lord.
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله المعلم : لا فخر في سيادتي ولد آدم وإنما فخري بمن سودني

SULAMI:v2p263#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r5.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r5.claim: True God-wariness is the state of one detached from all created things and turned toward God.
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r5.anchor: قال جعفر : هو التقى على الحقيقة والمتقى المنقطع عن الأكوان إلى الله

SULAMI:v2p263#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r6.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r6.claim: The noble person avoids associating partners with God, then avoids sins; the virtue within taqwa is knowledge of God, which has no endpoint, and growing knowledge brings growing fear and nobility with God.
SULAMI:v2p263#4/r6.anchor: قال أبو عثمان في قوله : ﴿ أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم ﴾ قال الكريم من يتقي الشرك

ITQAN:v1p91/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p91/r2.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
ITQAN:v1p91/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi uses 92:17 with 49:13 to argue that Abu Bakr is the best person after the Messenger.
ITQAN:v1p91/r2.anchor: وقد استدل بها الإمام فخر الدين الرازي مع قوله

ITQAN:v1p57/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p57/r1.claim: The verse about humanity's common origin was revealed in Mecca on the conquest day but is classified Medinan because it came after the Hijra; 5:3 is another example.
ITQAN:v1p57/r1.anchor: مثال ما نزل بمكة وحكمه مدني

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r1.claim: The claim that merit rests on piety rather than inherited rank is a sound rational meaning shared by people across generations; the Qur’an gives its finest expression.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r1.anchor: وأعلى مناسبة وأنورها وأجلها وأفخرها قول الله تعالى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r2.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r2.claim: The Prophet says that a person whose deeds hold him back will not be advanced by his lineage.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r2.anchor: وقول النبي من أبطأ به عمله لم يسرع به نسبه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r3.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r3.claim: The Prophet tells the Banu Hashim that people will come to him with deeds, while they must not come relying on lineage.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r3.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام يا بني هاشم لا تجيئني الناس بالأعمال وتجيئوني بالأنساب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r4.claim: Without acquired virtues and notable deeds, an ancestor would have no earned distinction for descendants to invoke in a comparison of merit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r4.anchor: لما كان أولا ولكان العلم من أمره مجهلا ولما تصور افتخار الثاني بالانتماء إليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r5.claim: The saying that all descend from Adam, who was made from dust, further undercuts inherited descent as a basis for superiority.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r5.anchor: ولذلك قال كلكم لآدم وآدم من التراب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r6.claim: A cited poetic maxim says inherited standing counts only when matched by merit a person acquires for himself.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p228/r6.anchor: وما الحسب الموروث لا دردره بمحتسب إلا بآخر مكتسب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Mulayka reports that after Bilal called the prayer from atop the Kaaba at the conquest, people objected to a Black enslaved man doing so; the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة قال لما كان يوم الفتح رقى بلال على ظهر الكعبة فأذن

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن أبي داود
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r3.claim: A report found in Ibn Bishkuwal’s handwriting attributes the verse to Abu Hind: the Prophet urged Banu Bayada to marry him to one of their women, and they objected to giving their daughters to freedmen.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p198#2/r3.anchor: وجدت بخط ابن بشكوال أن أبا بكر ابن أبي داود أخرج في تفسير له أنها نزلت في أبي هند

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the verse to Thabit ibn Qays’s insult toward a man who had not made room for him; the Prophet taught that only faith and piety confer superiority.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس، وقوله في الرجل الذي لم يفسح له ابن فلانة؟

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r2.claim: Muqatil says that at the conquest, people disparaged Bilal for giving the call to prayer atop the Kaaba; Gabriel informed the Prophet, who questioned them, and the verse rebuked them.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بلالا حتى أذن

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi says the verse rebukes boasting about lineage or wealth and looking down on the poor.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r3.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية وزجرهم عن التفاخر بالأنساب والتكاثر بالأموال والازدراء بالفقراء.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r4.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r4.claim: Ibn Abi Mulayka reports that people objected to a Black enslaved man calling the prayer from the Kaaba and said God would replace him if displeased; the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r4.anchor: أخبرنا ابن أبي مليكة قال: لما كان يوم الفتح رقى بلال على ظهر الكعبة فأذن، فقال بعض الناس:

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r5.speaker: يزيد بن شجرة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r5.claim: Yazid ibn Shajara reports that a Black youth was bought on condition he could pray behind the Prophet; the Prophet cared for and buried him, stirring envy among the Emigrants and Helpers before this verse came down.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p394/r5.anchor: وقال يزيد بن شجرة: مر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذات يوم ببعض الأسواق بالمدينة وإذا غلام أسود قائم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p396/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p396/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p396/r1.claim: The verse reminds the audience that all people descend from one father and one woman, and that piety is the measure of honor before God.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p396/r1.anchor: يعني أنكم بنو أب واحد وامرأة واحدة

DAMGHANI:v1p365/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r18.claim: Qabāʾil means tribes; the gloss also associates tribes and clans with heads.
DAMGHANI:v1p365/r18.anchor: القبيل جمع القبيلة قوله سبحانه في سورة الحجرات وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل لتعارفوا والقبائل والافخاذ يعني الرؤوس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.claim: The first Quranic sense is excellence or superiority, including God’s honoring Adam’s children and the noble book, messenger, and person.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r2.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الكريم في القرآن على ستة أوجه

FARRA:v3p71/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p71/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p71/r7.claim: The verse about human origins and peoples was also revealed in connection with the same incident.
FARRA:v3p71/r7.anchor: إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى وجعلناكم شعوبا

FARRA:v3p71/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p71/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p71/r8.claim: Shuʿūb are larger groupings than qabāʾil, which in turn are larger than afkhādh, clans or branches.
FARRA:v3p71/r8.anchor: والشعوب أكبر من القبائل، والقبائل أكبر من الأفخاذ

FARRA:v3p71/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p71/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p71/r9.claim: The purpose is that people recognize one another by lineage.

FARRA:v3p71/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p71/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p71/r10.claim: Inna is read with kasra because the statement about the most honored is not governed by the purpose clause li-taʿārafū.
FARRA:v3p71/r10.anchor: (إن أكرمكم) مكسورة لم يقع عليها التعارف

FARRA:v3p72/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p72/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p72/r1.claim: People are to know one another; the best in God's sight are the most Godfearing.
FARRA:v3p72/r1.anchor: لتعارفوا بينكم، وخيركم عند الله أتقاكم

FARRA:v3p72/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p72/r2.speaker: ثابت
FARRA:v3p72/r2.claim: Thabit says he will never again boast to anyone about his lineage.
FARRA:v3p72/r2.anchor: فقال ثابت: والله لا أفاخر رجلا في حسبه أبدا.

FARRA:v3p72/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p72/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p72/r3.claim: With fatḥa on أن, the sense is to recognize the pious noble; directly this would be لتعرفوا, though an elided purpose clause also permits the reading.
FARRA:v3p72/r3.anchor: ومن فتح: أن أكرمكم فكأنه قال: لتعارفوا أن الكريم المتقي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.claim: Karīm can mean noble, honored, or excellent: the most God-fearing are best, humanity is honored, and the other examples describe rank or honor.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r1.anchor: الكريم: الشريف الفاضل، قال الله تعالى: إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم [الحجرات: 13]

MAJAZ:v2p220/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p220/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p220/r3.claim: A shaʿb is a broad tribal grouping, with qabāʾil below it; he illustrates the usage with Ibn Aḥmar’s lines and al-Kumayt’s image of Nizār’s many divisions.
MAJAZ:v2p220/r3.anchor: يقال: من أي شعب أنت؟ فيقول من مضر من ربيعة، والقبائل دون ذلك

MAJAZ:v2p220/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p220/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p220/r4.claim: Li-taʿārafū completes the preceding clause; inn akramakum starts a new sentence, while a connected construction would use an in an akramakum.
MAJAZ:v2p220/r4.anchor: من الآية الأولى ثم ابتدأت «إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم» (13) ولو عملت لقلت أن أكرمكم عند الله.

NAHHAS:v4p215/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p215/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p215/r1.claim: The opening address is general, while the following reference to peoples and tribes is specific to Arabs.
NAHHAS:v4p215/r1.anchor: عام والذي بعده خاص لأن الشعوب والقبائل في العرب خاصة

NAHHAS:v4p215/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p215/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن
NAHHAS:v4p215/r2.claim: A report through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says the best person is one with a long life and good deeds.
NAHHAS:v4p215/r2.anchor: روى عبد الرحمن في العرب خاصة قيل يا رسول الله من خير الناس قال من طال عمره وحسن عمله

NAHHAS:v4p215/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p215/r3.speaker: درة
NAHHAS:v4p215/r3.claim: Durra reports that the Prophet named as best those who enjoin right, forbid wrong, maintain kinship, and are most God-fearing.
NAHHAS:v4p215/r3.anchor: وقالت درة سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من خير الناس قال آأمرهم بالمعروف وأنهاهم عن المنكر وأوصلهم للرحم وأتقاهم

NAHHAS:v4p215/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p215/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p215/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people abandoned this verse and instead claimed superiority by lineage.
NAHHAS:v4p215/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس ترك الناس هذه الآية

NAHHAS:v4p215/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p215/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
NAHHAS:v4p215/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that a caller on Judgment Day will summon the God-fearing to stand, and only they will rise.
NAHHAS:v4p215/r5.anchor: قال أبو هريرة ينادي مناد يوم القيامة إني جعلت نسبا وجعلهم نسبا

SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r1.claim: A shaʿb is the highest genealogical level; Arab lineage has six nested levels, with some adding عشيرة after فخذ to make seven.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r1.anchor: الشعوب: جمع شعب وهو أعلى طبقات الأنساب، وذلك أن طبقات النسب التي عليها العرب ست:

SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r2.claim: Shaʿb is named for the branching of tribes from it, and qabāʾil for their facing one another, like opposed sections of the head.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r2.anchor: وسمي الشعب شعبا لتشعب القبائل منه، والقبائل سميت بذلك لتقابلها، شبهت بقبائل الرأس وهي قطع متقابلة.

SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r3.claim: Alternative interpretations say peoples are non-Arabs and tribes Arabs, with asbāṭ for Israelites; another says shaʿb is distant ancestry and qabila near ancestry.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r3.anchor: وقيل: الشعوب في العجم، والقبائل في العرب، والأسباط في بني إسرائيل. وقيل: الشعب النسب الأبعد،

SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r4.claim: A cited, unattributed poem speaks of noble and worthy members among tribes from different peoples.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r4.anchor: وأنشد: 4086 قبائل من شعوب ليس فيهم كريم قد يعد ولا نجيب

SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r5.claim: The nisba شعوبية, with fatḥ on shīn, names a group hostile to Arabs.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13/r5.anchor: والنسب إلى الشعب " شعوبية " بفتح الشين، وهم جيل يبغضون العرب.

SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r1.claim: Most readers lighten لتعارفوا by deleting one of the two original tāʾs; al-Bazzi doubles it, and al-Aʿmash retains both tāʾs.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r1.anchor: العامة على تخفيف التاء، والأصل: لتتعارفوا فحذف إحدى التاءين. والبزي بتشديدها.

SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reads لتعرفوا, from عرف.

SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r3.claim: The purpose-lām in لتعارفوا attaches to جعلناكم.

SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r4.claim: The common reading has kasra in إن; Ibn Abbas reads it with fatḥ, opening a different syntactic analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r4.anchor: والعامة على كسر " إن أكرمكم ". وابن عباس على فتحها:

SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r5.claim: With Ibn Abbas's fatḥ, if lām is imperative—which is unlikely—أن أكرمكم can be the object of معرفة. If lām is purposive, the object is omitted: know the truth because the most honored is the most God-fearing.
SAMIN-DURR:49:13#2/r5.anchor: فإن جعلت اللام لام الأمر وفيه بعد اتضح أن يكون قوله: " أن أكرمكم " بالفتح مفعول العرفان،

ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r6.claim: All people descend from Adam and Eve and share one father and one mother.
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r6.anchor: خلقناكم من آدم وحواء، وكلكم بنو أب واحد وأم واحدة إليهما ترجعون

ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r7.claim: A shaʿb is larger than a tribe.
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r7.anchor: والشعب أعظم من القبيلة. أي لم يجعلكم

ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r8.claim: God made people into peoples and tribes so that they would recognize one another, not boast over one another.
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r8.anchor: أي لم يجعلكم شعوبا وقبائل لتفاخروا وإنما جعلناكم كذلك لتتعارفوا

ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r9.claim: The highest rank with God belongs to the most pious.
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r9.anchor: ثم أعلمهم الله - عز وجل - أن أرفعهم عنده منزلة أتقاهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r10.claim: The clause may also be read with anna, yielding the sense that God made people tribes so they might know one another, that the most noble before God is the most pious.
ZAJJAJ:v5p37/r10.anchor: ولو قرئت " أن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم " جاز ذلك

ASAD-NOTES:49:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:49:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:49:intro/r3.claim: The discourse moves toward the brotherhood of believers and, in the widest sense, the brotherhood of all humanity.
ASAD-NOTES:49:intro/r3.anchor: the principle of the brotherhood of all believe rs (verse 10) and, in its widest sense, the brotherhood of all mankind (verse 13)

ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n15/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n15/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n15/r1.claim: Following Zamakhshari, Razi, and Baydawi, Asad reads this as each person's origin in a father and mother, with shared biological origins implying equal human dignity.
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n15/r1.anchor: father and a mother" (Zamakhsharl, Razi, Baydiwl) - implying that this equality

ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r1.claim: Zamakhshari explains the purpose of human groups as recognizing that all people belong to one human family without inherent superiority.
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r1.anchor: without any inherent superiority of one over another (Zamakhshari).

ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r2.claim: This teaching connects with the previous two verses' exhortation to respect and safeguard one another's dignity.
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r2.anchor: This connects with the exhortation, in the preceding two verses, to respect and safeguard each other's dignity.

ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r3.claim: Human differences should deepen mutual understanding and appreciation of shared humanity; Asad condemns racial, national, and tribal prejudice, citing the Prophet's explicit condemnation.
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r3.anchor: is meant to foster rather than to diminish their mutual desire to understand and appreciate the essential human oneness underlying their outward differentiations

ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r4.speaker: the Prophet
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r4.claim: A hadith fragment cited by Tirmidhi and Abu Da'ud on Abu Hurayrah's authority says God removed pagan pride in ancestry; people are believers mindful of God or sinners, and all descend from Adam, made of dust.
ASAD-NOTES:49:13#n16/r4.anchor: the Prophet said: "Behold, God has removed from you the arrogance of pagan ignorance (1ahiliyyah) with its boast of ancestral glories.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r7.claim: Pride in clan, family, or creed is a jāhiliyyah remnant that Muslims must abandon.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r7.anchor: Pride and vanity about one’s clan, family or creed are relics

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r8.claim: All humanity comes from one pair, Adam and Eve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r8.anchor: The Almighty has created all mankind from a single pair of man and woman: Adam and Eve.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r9.claim: Human groups and tribes were made for mutual identification, not to establish superiority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r9.anchor: The real aim behind dividing mankind into various groups and tribes is merely to identify each separately.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r10.claim: Piety, rather than clan or tribal affiliation, is the basis of honor before God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p398/r10.anchor: The basis of honour in the sight of God is piety and not association with a particular clan or tribe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p414/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p414/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p414/r5.claim: Verse 7 describes God’s arrangement to save Muslims from disbelief, defiance, and disobedience; the following prohibitions prevent social poison that could turn believers described as merciful to one another into enemies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p414/r5.anchor: In verse seven earlier, the Almighty has mentioned the elaborate arrangement He had made to save Muslims out of His grace

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r1.claim: Unchecked social mischief from the prohibited conduct poisons society and can turn those God called merciful to one another into enemies.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r1.anchor: which if not stopped, causes those who have been called

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r2.claim: The address to believers is pointed: the ensuing evils are fisq and contrary to faith, so people who embraced faith should not stain themselves with fisq.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p415/r2.anchor: not merely meant for address; further down the evils which are fisq and also contrary to faith are mentioned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r3.claim: Ridicule grows from Satan’s trial of superiority by race, creed, family, and tribe, which makes people regard others as inferior and eventually turns into custom or even supposed religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r3.anchor: Among the various evils invented by Satan to mislead man is the trial of superiority of one’s race, creed, family and tribe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r4.claim: Brahmans, Israelite Levites, and Arab Quraysh acquired privileged sacred status; this superiority persists across nations, including Muslim tribes that now regard themselves as better than others.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r4.anchor: Thus the Brahmans in the Hindus, the Levites in the Israelites and the Quraysh in the Arabs had acquired a holy status for themselves

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r6.claim: The section’s final verse points to the inner source of the forbidden mockery and related evils: claims of racial, familial, or tribal superiority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p416/r6.anchor: The verse which is coming up at the end of this section points to this inner aspect.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r2.claim: Honor rests on faith and piety, not race, clan, family, tribe, nation, or wealth; God will judge who is truly noble, and lineage-based vanity has no standing before Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r2.anchor: the basis of honour and respect is not race, clan, family, tribe and nation or riches; the real basis is a person’s faith and piety

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r8.claim: In jāhiliyyah, Arabs prized poets and orators who exalted their tribe and humiliated others, preventing unity; Islam introduced faith-based brotherhood, made them world leaders, and warned them to honor that gift.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p417/r8.anchor: A poet and orator would be considered as the greatest in his nation if he was unrivalled in eulogizing the superiority of his nation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r5.claim: The universal address uproots pride in lineage, family, and tribe: all humanity descends from Adam and Eve and no one is superior by species.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r5.anchor: they are the progeny of one man and woman: all mankind was created from Adam and Eve

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r6.claim: Families and tribes exist so people can identify one another, like distinctions of appearance, color, and physique; these divisions confer no further status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p421/r6.anchor: families and tribes so that people can recognize one another. It has no significance beyond this.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r1.claim: Honor before God depends on taqwā: the most honored is most mindful of Him and vigilant in observing His bounds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r1.anchor: The basis of respect in the sight of God is taqwā.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r2.claim: God knows every person’s words and deeds and can honor an unknown person of low origin while casting an unworthy person from Quraysh or the Hashimites into the pit he deserves.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p422/r2.anchor: He who is worthy of respect shall certainly gain a place of respect however unknown and of lowly origin he may be.

NASHR:v2p231/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p231/r5.speaker: البزي
NASHR:v2p231/r5.claim: The section lists 31 future verbs whose initial tāʾ may double, across the cited passages; al-Bazzi transmits doubling in the stated routes, including the forms at 20:69 and 49:13.
NASHR:v2p231/r5.anchor: وذلك في إحدى وثلاثين تاء، وهي ولا تيمموا الخبيث هنا،

QIRAAT-ER:49:13:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:49:13:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:49:13:16#1/r1.claim: Assimilation of the Form VI prefix tāʾ into lām is phonetic and does not change meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:49:13:16#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of tāʾ — phonetic variant, no semantic change; the tāʾ of the Form VI prefix

AZRAQI:v1p274/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r1.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
AZRAQI:v1p274/r1.claim: Ibn Abī Mulayka reports that at the conquest some objected to the Black Bilāl calling the adhān on the Kaaba and said God would change the matter if displeased; the verse was revealed.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة قال لما كان يوم الفتح رقى بلال فأذن على ظهر الكعبة

AZRAQI:v1p274/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r2.speaker: أشياخ الواقدي
AZRAQI:v1p274/r2.claim: Al-Wāqidī's shaykhs place the event at noon on the conquest day: the Prophet ordered Bilāl to call prayer from the Kaaba while Quraysh hid on the hills, fearing execution or seeking safety.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r2.anchor: عن الواقدي عن أشياخه قالوا جاءت الظهر يوم الفتح فأمر رسول الله & بلالا أن يؤذن بالظهر فوق ظهر الكعبة

AZRAQI:v1p274/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r3.speaker: جويرية بنت أبي جهل
AZRAQI:v1p274/r3.claim: Juwairiya says Bilāl has indeed raised the Prophet's renown; she will pray but will never love those who killed her loved ones, and says her father rejected prophethood rather than oppose his tribe.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r3.anchor: تقول جويرية بنت أبي جهل قد لعمري رفع لك ذكرك أما الصلاة فسنصلي

AZRAQI:v1p274/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r4.speaker: خالد بن أسيد
AZRAQI:v1p274/r4.claim: Khālid ibn Asīd thanks God that his father died the day before the conquest and did not hear Bilāl's call from the Kaaba.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r4.anchor: وقال خالد بن أسيد الحمد الله الذي أكرم أبي فلم يسمع بهذا اليوم وكان أسيد مات قبل الفتح بيوم

AZRAQI:v1p274/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r5.speaker: الحارث بن هشام
AZRAQI:v1p274/r5.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām cries out in shame and wishes he had died before hearing Bilāl call above the Kaaba.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r5.anchor: وقال الحارث بن هاشم واثكلاه ليتني مت قبل أن أسمع بلالا ينهق فوق الكعبة

AZRAQI:v1p274/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r6.speaker: الحكم بن أبي العاص
AZRAQI:v1p274/r6.claim: Al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ calls it a momentous event that a slave of Banū Jumah should call from the Kaaba structure.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r6.anchor: وقال الحكم بن أبي العاص هذا والله الحدث الجليل أن يصبح عبد بني جمح ينهق على بنية أبي طلحة

AZRAQI:v1p274/r7.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r7.speaker: سهيل بن عمرو
AZRAQI:v1p274/r7.claim: Suhayl ibn ʿAmr says that if the event angers God, God will change it.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r7.anchor: وقال سهيل بن عمرو إن كان هذا سخطا لله فسيغيره الله

AZRAQI:v1p274/r8.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r8.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
AZRAQI:v1p274/r8.claim: Abū Sufyān says he will say nothing because a pebble would report it; Gabriel tells the Prophet the men's remarks, and the Prophet repeats them to the group. Abū Sufyān denies speaking, and the Prophet laughs.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r8.anchor: وقال أبو سفيان بن حرب أما أنا فلا أقول شيئا لو قلت شيئا لأخبرته هذه الحصاة فأتى جبريل عليه السلام رسول الله

AZRAQI:v1p274/r9.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p274/r9.speaker: أبو الوليد
AZRAQI:v1p274/r9.claim: Abū al-Walīd says Bilāl belonged to orphans of Banū al-Sabbāq of ʿAbd al-Dār, whose father entrusted him to Umayya ibn Khalaf, Bilāl's torturer; Bilāl's brother was named Kuḥayl.
AZRAQI:v1p274/r9.anchor: قال أبو الوليد وكان بلال لأيتام من بني السباق ابن عبد الدار أوصى به أبوهم إلى أمية بن خلف الجمحي

IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r1.speaker: صفية بنت شيبة
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r1.claim: Safiyya bint Shayba reports that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet circled the Kaaba seven times on his camel, took its key, entered, and broke a wooden dove inside.
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r1.anchor: عن صفية بنت شيبة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزل مكة، واطمأن الناس، خرج حتى جاء البيت

IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq relays anonymously from some scholars that the Prophet told Quraysh God had removed lineage pride, all people descend from Adam and dust, and the verse makes piety the measure of honor.
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فحدثني بعض أهل العلم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قام على باب الكعبة

IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r3.claim: The address places old claims to distinction, blood, or property under the Prophet's feet, except the Kaaba's custodianship and water service for pilgrims.
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r3.anchor: ألا كل مأثرة أو دم أو مال يدعى فهو تحت قدمي هاتين إلا سدانة البيت وسقاية الحاج

IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r4.claim: For mistaken quasi-intentional killing with a whip or stick, the address sets an aggravated blood payment of one hundred camels, forty carrying young.
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r4.anchor: وقتيل الخطأ شبه العمد بالسوط والعصا، ففيه الدية مغلظة، مائة من الإبل، أربعون منها في بطونها أولادها

IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r5.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNHISHAM:v2p411#2/r5.claim: When Quraysh ask what he will do to them, the Prophet calls them a good, noble brother and nephew and releases them.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p233/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p233/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p233/r1.claim: Qatāda explains “peoples” as distant ancestry and “tribes” as nearer lineage, as in saying someone belongs to a particular clan's descendants.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p233/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وجعلناكم شعوبا ﴾ قال هو النسب البعيد قال والقبائل كما سمعته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r1.speaker: الحارث بن هشام وعتاب بن أسيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r1.claim: One report says al-Harith ibn Hisham and ʿAttab ibn Asid were angered when Bilal called the adhan atop the Kaaba at the conquest of Mecca, and the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r1.anchor: قيل: غضب الحارث بن هشام وعتاب بن أسيد حين أذن بلال يوم فتح مكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the occasion was Thabit ibn Qays calling a man who failed to make room for him son of so-and-so; the Prophet rebuked him that superiority is only through religion and piety, and the command to make room also came down then.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس، سببها قول ثابت بن قيس لرجل لم يفسح له عند النبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r3.claim: The phrase means either Adam and Eve or that each person comes from a father and mother; all are equal in this respect, so there is no basis for boasting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r3.anchor: من ذكر وأنثى: أي من آدم وحواء، أو كل أحد منكم من أب وأم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r4.claim: One view identifies shuʿub with non-Arabs, qabaʾil with Arabs, and asbat with the children of Israel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r4.anchor: وقيل: الشعوب في العجم والقبائل في العرب، والأسباط في بني إسرائيل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r5.claim: Another view makes the shuʿub the Arabs of Yemen descended from Qahtan, and the tribes Rabiʿa, Mudar, and the rest of Adnan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r5.anchor: وقيل: الشعوب: عرب اليمن من قحطان، والقبائل: ربيعة ومضر وسائر عدنان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r6.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r6.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak say a shaʿb is the more remote lineage and a tribe the nearer one; the cited poem contrasts tribes drawn from peoples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة، ومجاهد، والضحاك: الشعب: النسب الأبعد، والقبيلة: الأقرب، قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r7.claim: Another view defines shuʿub as clients and qabaʾil as Arabs.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r8.speaker: أبو روق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r8.claim: Abu Rawq says shuʿub are those affiliated with towns and villages, while qabaʾil are those affiliated with their fathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r8.anchor: وقال أبو روق: الشعوب: الذين ينسبون إلى المدائن والقرى، والقبائل: الذين ينسبون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r9.claim: The singular of shuʿub is shaʿb with fatḥa on the shīn; a separate Shaʿb is a branch of Hamdan, linked to the Successor ʿAmir al-Shaʿbi, and shuʿubiyya denotes non-Arab peoples or those favoring them over Arabs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r9.anchor: وواحد الشعوب شعب، بفتح الشين. وشعب: بطن من همدان ينسب إليه عامر الشعبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r10.claim: Abu ʿUbayda is described as a Kharijite shuʿubi with a book on Arab merits; Ibn Gharbasa wrote for non-Arab superiority, prompting several rebuttals by Andalusi scholars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r10.anchor: وكان أبو عبيدة خارجيا شعوبيا، وله كتاب في مناقب العرب، ولابن غرسبة رسالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r11.speaker: الجمهور والأعمش ومجاهد وابن كثير وابن محيصن وابن عباس وأبان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r11.claim: The majority read لتعارفوا with one deleted tāʾ; al-Aʿmash keeps two tāʾs, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir in one transmission, and Ibn Muhaysin assimilate them, while Ibn Abbas and Aban from Asim read لتعرفوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لتعارفوا، مضارع تعارف، محذوف التاء والأعمش: بتاءين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r12.claim: The purpose is to know one another by lineage, not claim descent from someone other than one's fathers or boast of ancestors; distinction is by piety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522/r12.anchor: والمعنى: أنكم جعلكم الله تعالى ما ذكر، كي يعرف بعضكم بعضا في النسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r1.claim: In his conquest-of-Mecca sermon, the Prophet said people are either a pious believer honored by God or a wicked wretch lowly before God, then recited the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r1.anchor: وفي خطبته عليه الصلاة والسلام يوم فتح مكة: «إنما الناس رجلان، مؤمن تقي كريم على الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r2.claim: The Prophet said whoever wants to be the noblest of people should fear God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r2.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من سره أن يكون أكرم الناس فليتق الله»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r3.claim: People boast of ancestry, regions, schools, learning, and crafts; the author especially criticizes descendants of Sufi lodge shaykhs who trade on their fathers' virtue despite lacking it themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r3.anchor: وما زال التفاخر بالأنساب في الجاهلية والإسلام، وبالبلاد وبالمذاهب وبالعلوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r4.claim: The author cites satirical poetry about people boasting of ancestors' distant, decayed branches rather than their own merit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r4.anchor: وأعجب شيء إلى عاقل ... فروع عن المجد مسأخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r5.claim: The majority read إن with kasra, while Ibn Abbas reads with fatḥa; his reading لتعرفوا permits different grammatical constructions for the clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إن، بكسر الهمزة وابن عباس: بفتحها، وكان قرأ: لتعرفوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r6.claim: With Ibn Abbas's فتح reading, إن may depend on لتعرفوا with the lām as imperative, which best fits the sense; if the lām is purposive, the construction is awkward unless تعرفوا has an omitted object such as الحق.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p522#2/r6.anchor: فاحتمل أن تكون أن معمولة لتعرفوا، وتكون اللام في لتعرفوا لام الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r1.claim: All people descend from Adam and Eve and are equal in that origin, so lineage is no basis for boasting.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r1.anchor: من آدم وحواء عليهما السلام فالكل سواء في ذلك فلا وجه للتفاخر بالنسب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r2.claim: A poetic saying expresses the same equality: people are peers, with Adam as father and Eve as mother.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r2.anchor: الناس في عالم التمثيل أكفاء أبوهم آدم والأم حواء

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that each person was created from one father and one mother; the author finds it weak because it does not explain the rebuke of lineage pride.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المراد هنا إنا خلقنا كل واحد منكم من أب وأم ويبعده عدم ظهور ترتب ذم التفاخر بالنسب عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r4.claim: A further view takes the phrase as establishing brotherhood that bars backbiting; its connection to what follows is less strong than the shared-origin explanation, though the brotherhood point is clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو تقرير للأخوة المانعة عن الأغتياب وعدم ظهور الترتب عليه على حاله

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r5.claim: In the main genealogical usage, a shaʿb is a great group tracing to one ancestor and encompassing tribes; a tribe encompasses ʿamāʾir, then clans, subclans, and families. The author illustrates the ranks with Khuzaima, Kinana, Quraysh, Qusayy, Hashim, and al-Abbas.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r5.anchor: وهم الجمع العظيم المنتسبون إلى أصل واحد وهو يجمع القبائل والقبيلة تجمع العمائر والعمارة بفتح العين وقد تكسر تجمع البطون

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r6.speaker: بعض الأدباء
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r6.claim: A literary poet lists the descent order as tribe, shaʿb, ʿimāra, clan, and subclan, then says a man is sheltered by his family and an arrow needs its feathers to fly straight.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r6.anchor: قبيلة فوقها شعب وبعدها عمارة ثم بطن تلوه فخذ وليس يؤوي الفتى إلا فصيلته

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r7.claim: Another poem adds ʿashira after family and recites the sequence from shaʿb through tribe, ʿimāra, clan, subclan, family, and ʿashira.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r7.anchor: أقصد الشعب فهو أكثر حي عددا في الحساب ثم القبيلة ثم يتلوهما العمارة ثم البطن

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r8.claim: The name shuʿub is explained by the tribes branching out from them.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن ابن الكلبي عن أبيه
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r9.claim: A lineage ranking relayed by Abu Ubayda from Ibn al-Kalbi and his father places the family before ʿimāra and ʿimāra before subclan, unlike the preceding arrangement.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r9.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيدة عن ابن الكلبي عن أبيه تقديم الشعب ثم القبيلة ثم الفصيلة ثم العمارة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r10.speaker: مسروق
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r10.claim: Masruq relates that a man from the shuʿub became Muslim and was charged jizya; al-Alusi cites this to support the non-Arab interpretation of shuʿub.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r10.anchor: وأيد كون الشعوب في العجم ما في حديث مسروق أن رجلا من الشعوب أسلم فكانت تؤخذ منه الجزية

ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r11.claim: One possibility makes shuʿub the plural of shuʿubi: someone, such as a Jew or Magian, who belittles Arabs and denies their superiority; Abu Ubayda wrote a book attacking Arabs, and Ibn Garsiya argued for non-Arabs, prompting Andalusian refutations.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p161#3/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع الشعوبي وهو الذي يصغر شأن العرب ولا يرى لهم فضلا على غيرهم كيهود ومجوس

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r1.claim: One view identifies shuʿub with the Arabs of Yemen descended from Qahtan and the tribes with Rabiʿa, Mudar, and the rest of Adnan.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r1.anchor: وقيل : الشعوب عرب اليمن من قحطان والقبائل ربيعة ومضر وسائر عدنان

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r2.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r2.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak say shaʿb denotes the more remote ancestry and qabila the nearer.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك : الشعب النسب إلا بعد والقبيلة الأقرب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r3.claim: Another view takes shuʿub as non-Arab clients and qabilas as Arabs.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r4.speaker: أبو روق
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r4.claim: Abu Rawq says shuʿub are those tracing ancestry to towns and villages, while Arab tribes trace themselves to fathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r4.anchor: وقال أبو روق : الشعوب الذين ينتسبون إلى المدائن والقرى والقبائل العرب الذين ينتسبون إلى آبائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r5.claim: The purpose of the social groupings is mutual recognition, kinship ties, identifying genealogies, and inheritance, not boasting about forebears and tribes; this restriction is inferred from what is specified and what is left unsaid.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r5.anchor: علة للجعل أي جعلناكم كذلك ليعرف بعضكم بعضا فتصلوا الأرحام وتبينوا الأنساب والتوارث لا لتفاخروا بالآباء والقبائل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r6.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads litataʿarafu with two tāʾs, preserving the original form.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ( لتتعارفوا ) بتاءين على الأصل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r7.speaker: مجاهد وابن كثير في رواية وابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r7.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Kathir in one transmission, and Ibn Muhaysin assimilate the two tāʾs.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r7.anchor: ومجاهد وابن كثير في رواية وابن محيصن بإدغام التاء في التاء

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وأبان عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Aban from Asim read li-taʿrafu with kasra on the rāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r8.anchor: وابن عباس وأبان عن عاصم ( لتعرفوا ) بكسر الراء

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r9.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r9.claim: Ibn Jinni says the object of taʿrafu is omitted, as in the poetic line meaning that a person learns only in order to know what he has learned; the author estimates the object as the kinship among you.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r9.anchor: قال ابن جني : والمفعول محذوف أي لتعرفوا ما أنتم محتاجون إليه كقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r10.claim: This clause justifies rejecting lineage pride: the most honored and highest in rank before God in this life and the next is the most God-fearing, so anyone seeking high rank should pursue taqwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r10.anchor: تعليل للنهي عن التفاخر بالأنساب المستفاد من الكلام بطريق الأستئناف الحقيقي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reads anna with fatḥa, supplying a causal lām: they should not boast by ancestry because the most honored before God is the most pious.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ( أن ) بفتح الهمزة على حذف لام التعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r12.claim: Al-Bahr reports Ibn Abbas reading both li-taʿrafu and anna-akramakum; it suggests the latter clause is the object of an imperative li-taʿrafu, which the author finds semantically better than a causal lām. A causal reading could work if the omitted object is al-haqq.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p162/r12.anchor: وفي البحر أن ابن عباس قرأ ( لتعرفوا وأنأكرمكم ) بفتح الهمزة فاحتمل أن يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r1.claim: God is knowing of people and their deeds, and fully aware of their inward states.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r2.claim: A conquest-of-Mecca occasion report says al-Harith ibn Hisham and Attab ibn Asid objected angrily when Bilal called the prayer from atop the Kaaba, calling him a black slave; this verse then came down.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r2.anchor: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أذن بلال على الكعبة فغضب الحرث بن هشام وعتاب بن أسيد

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas gives as occasion that Thabit ibn Qays insulted a man who did not make room before the Prophet by calling him the son of a certain woman; the Prophet rebuked him and said superiority is only through religion and taqwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس سبب نزولها قول ثابت بن قيس لرجل لم يفسح له عند النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يا ابن فلانة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r4.speaker: الزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r4.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that the Prophet instructed Banu Bayada to marry Abu Hind, his cupper, to a woman among them; they objected to marrying their daughters to clients, and the verse was revealed, specifically for Abu Hind according to al-Zuhri.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r4.anchor: عن الزهري قال : أمر رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بني بياضة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r5.speaker: عروة عن عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r5.claim: A report through Urwa from Aisha says the Prophet commanded that Abu Hind be married into a family and that a woman be married to him, after which this verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r5.anchor: عن عروة عن عائشة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : أنكحوا أبا هند

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r6.speaker: يزيد بن شجرة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r6.claim: Yazid ibn Shajara relates that the Prophet bought a black boy who required that he not be kept from the five prayers behind him; after the boy fell ill and died, the Prophet washed and buried him, deeply affecting the Emigrants and Helpers, and the verse was revealed. The author doubts the report's soundness.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r6.anchor: وعن يزيد بن شجرة مر رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r7.claim: The verse rules out pride in ancestry, as prophetic reports also make clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r7.anchor: وقد دلت على أنه لا ينبغي التفاخر بالأنساب وبذلك نطقت الأخبار

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r8.claim: Ibn Umar reports that at the conquest the Prophet praised God for removing pre-Islamic disgrace and arrogance, said people are either pious and noble before God or sinful and low, and affirmed that all are children of Adam created from dust before reciting this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طاف يوم الفتح على راحلته

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r9.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r9.claim: Jabir says the Prophet declared in the Farewell Sermon that the Lord is one, no Arab or non-Arab and no black or red person has precedence over another except by taqwa, then asked witnesses to convey the message.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r9.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله قال : خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وسط أيام التشريق

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r10.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r10.claim: Abu Umama reports the Prophet saying God removed the arrogance of pre-Islamic lineage, all people descend from Adam and Eve, and the most honored is the most pious; he also urged marriage to a suitor whose religion and trustworthiness are approved.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r10.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله أذهب نخوة الجاهلية وتكبرها بآبائها

ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r11.speaker: أحمد وجماعة
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r11.claim: Ahmad and others transmit a similar report, but omit the instruction about marrying a suitor whose religion and trustworthiness are approved.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p163/r11.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وجماعة نحوه لكن ليس فيه فمن أتاكم الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r1.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet saying all people descend from Adam, made from dust, and warning against boasting of forefathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r1.anchor: وأخرج البزاز عن حذيفة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلكم بنو آدم وآدم خلق من تراب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God's address at Resurrection: God made piety the measure of honor, but people clung to worldly lineages; God will raise His lineage and abase theirs.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r2.anchor: وأخرج اتلطبراني وابن مردويه عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : يقول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r3.claim: Al-Khatib transmits from Ali a similar report raised to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r3.anchor: وأخرج الخطيب عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه نحوه مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r4.claim: Abu Rayhana reports the Prophet warning that one who claims nine unbelieving forefathers for pride will be the tenth in Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r4.anchor: عن أبي ريحانه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من انتسب إلى تسعة باء كفار

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r5.claim: Asked who is most honored, the Prophet answers the most pious, then Joseph, and says the best Arabs remain best in Islam if they gain understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r5.anchor: وأخرج البخاري والنسائي عن أبي هريرة قال : سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r6.claim: The verse rebuts pride in ancestry: lineage is unearned, as 53:39 says a person has only what he strives for; piety is the real distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r6.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى وجه رد التفاخر بالنسب حيث أفادت أن شرف النسب غير مكتسب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r7.claim: This principle does not deny collective differences in merit: reports rank Persians above Nabateans and Israelites above Copts.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r7.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي كون العرب أشرف من العجم وتفاوت كل من العرب والعجم في الشرف فقد ذكروا أن الفرس أشرف من النبط

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r8.claim: Wathila reports God's choice of Kinanah, Quraysh, Hashim, and the Prophet from successive lineages; Alusi attributes it to good qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r8.anchor: وأخرج مسلم وغيره عن واثلة بن الأسقع قال : قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله اصطفى كنانة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r9.claim: Collective merit of Arabs over non-Arabs does not mean every Arab surpasses every non-Arab individually.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r9.anchor: لا نعني بذلك أن كل عربي ممتاز على كل عجمي بالخصال الحميدة بل إن المجموع ممتاز على المجموع

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r10.speaker: جمع من الفقهاء
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r10.claim: A group of jurists call Fatima's descendants the noblest Arab lineage because they descend from the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r10.anchor: ثم إن أشرف العرب نسبا أولاد فاطمة رضي الله تعالى عنها لأنهم ينتسبون إلى النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r11.claim: Fatima reports the Prophet saying Adam's children attach to a male agnate except Fatima's children, for whom he is guardian and agnate.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r11.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن فاطمة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r12.claim: A report from Umar says daughters' children affiliate to their fathers except Fatima's children, whose agnate and father is the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r12.anchor: وفي رواية له عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه كل ابن انثى كان عصبتهم لأبيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r13.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r13.claim: The first Fatima report is marked hasan by al-Suyuti, but that grading is challenged; Alusi says its proof is not limited to that report.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r13.anchor: ورمز الجلال السيوطي للأول بأنه حسن وتعقب

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r14.claim: Al-Miswar reports the Prophet calling Fatima part of himself and saying all lineages end at Resurrection except his lineage and in-law ties.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r14.anchor: عن المسور بن مخرمة ولا كلام فيه قال : قال صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة بضعة مني

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r15.speaker: الشريف السمهودي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r15.claim: Al-Samhudi reasons Fatima's children are part of her and, through her, part of the Prophet, giving them exceptional honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r15.anchor: قال الشريف السمهودي : ومعلوم أن أولادها بضعة منها فيكونون بواسطتها بضعة منه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r16.speaker: الذهبي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r16.claim: Ibn Asakir's report from Umar says every lineage and affinity ends at Resurrection except the Prophet's; al-Dhahabi objects to Ibn Waki, but a hasan mursal version supports it.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r16.anchor: والذهبي وإن تعقبه بقوله : فيه ابن وكيع لا يعمد

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r17.speaker: المناوي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r17.claim: Al-Munawi concludes that affiliation by lineage to the Prophet has great benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r17.anchor: كما قال المناوي عظيم نفع الأنساب إليه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r18.claim: Warnings to the Prophet's family do not negate lineage honor; they prevent reliance on ancestry and urge taqwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r18.anchor: والمراد لا أغني عنكم شيئا بمجرد نفسي من غير ما يكرمني الله تعالى به من نحو شفاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r19.claim: The Prophet cannot benefit relatives by himself, apart from God's grant of intercession or forgiveness; he owns no benefit or harm independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p164/r19.anchor: والمراد لا أغني عنكم شيئا بمجرد نفسي من غير ما يكرمني الله تعالى به من نحو شفاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r1.claim: A person may identify himself as the Prophet's descendant when expressing gratitude or serving another legitimate purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r1.anchor: فعلى هذا لا بأس بقول الرجل : أنا من ذرية رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r2.speaker: ابن حجر
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r2.claim: Ibn Hajar says the ban on lineage boasting concerns arrogance and contempt for a Muslim.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r2.anchor: وقد نقل المناوي عن ابن حجر أنه قال نهيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن التفاخر

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r3.claim: Reports of God's choosing Kinanah and the Prophet's saying he is the Prophet and son of Abd al-Muttalib support mentioning noble descent.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r3.anchor: وعلى ما ذكرناه أولا جاء قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام إن الله اصطفى كنانة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r4.claim: Prophetic lineage must not be left devoid of piety or stained by desire; good deeds are better from the Prophet's house and sins worse.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r4.anchor: فالحسنة في نفسها حسنة وهي من بيت النبوة أحسن والسيئة في نفسها سيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r5.claim: Following desire may make a noble descendant ashamed of the Prophet and deny his ancestry.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r5.anchor: وقد يبلغ اتباع الهوى بذلك النسيب الشريف إلى حيث يستحي أن ينسب إلى رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r6.claim: A poem says deeds reveal true character and mocks the bad-behaving noble's claim to Ahmad's lineage.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r6.anchor: قيل لشريف سيء الأفعال : قال النبي مقال صدق لم يزل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r7.speaker: الشريف
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r7.claim: A Khurasan sharif insults a learned black freedman, boasting of Prophetic descent while people honor the scholar.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r7.anchor: وقال : يا أسود الحوافر والمشافر يا كافر ابن كافر

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r8.speaker: الشيخ
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r8.claim: The shaykh replies that the sharif darkened his inner self while he purified his; people treat each according to conduct like opposite ancestors.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r8.anchor: فقال الشيخ : لا تفعلوا هذا محتمل منه لجده ومعفو عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r9.claim: The proverb that Hashimite stock cannot help a Bahili soul means lineage cannot compensate for vile character; Bahila's descendants were reputedly base.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r9.anchor: ولا ينفع الأصل من هاشم إذا كانت النفس من باهلة أي لا ينفع في الامتياز

ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r10.speaker: عربي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r10.claim: An Arab is asked whether he would accept being Bahili and entering Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p165/r10.anchor: حتى قيل لعربي أترضى أن تكون باهليا وتدخل الجنة فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r1.speaker: عربي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r1.claim: The Arab answers that he would only accept if Paradise's people never discovered his ancestry; another saying says a dog howls when called Bahili.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r1.anchor: لا إلا بشرط أن لا يعلم أهل الجنة أني بأهلي وقيل : إذا قيل للكلب ياباهلي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r2.claim: Jurists excluded Bahila as an equal match for other Arabs, but Alusi questions the generalization.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r2.anchor: ولم يجعلهم الفقهاء لذلك أكفاء لغيرهم من العرب لكن لا يخلو ذلك من نظر

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r3.claim: The rule that Arabs are equal matches does not distinguish tribes, despite the Prophet's knowledge of their characters.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r3.anchor: فإن النص أعني إن العرب بعضهم أكفاء لبعض لم يفصل مع أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أعلم بقبائل العرب وأخلاقهم

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r4.claim: Marriage compatibility may turn on publicly recognized disgrace, even without an objective basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r4.anchor: مدار الكفاءة وعدمها على العار وعدمه في المعروف بين الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r5.claim: He compares this to rescinding a house purchase if people regard it as unlucky because that belief lowers market value.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r5.anchor: وهذا نظير ما ذكروا إذا اشترى الشخص دارا فتبين أن الناس يستشئمونها أنه بالخيار

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r6.claim: Lineage is considered in Islamic and pre-Islamic society, especially in marriage compatibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r6.anchor: وبالجملة شرف النسب مما اعتبر جاهلية وإسلاما أما جاهلية فأظهر من أن يبرهن عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r7.speaker: مالك والثوري والكرخي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r7.claim: Most jurists consider lineage in marriage compatibility; Malik, al-Thawri, al-Karkhi, and others opposed it, and reports supporting them are answered elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r7.anchor: في باب النكاح على الوجه المفصل في كتب الفقه ولم يخالف في ذلك فيما نعلم إلا الإمام مالك والثوري والكرخي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r8.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r8.claim: Al-Mawardi reports consensus that the supreme imam must be Qurayshi.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r8.anchor: من أنه يشترط فيها كون الإمام قرشيا وقد أجمعوا على ذلك كما قال الماوردي

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r9.speaker: ضرار وأبو بكر الباقلاني
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r9.claim: Darrar and al-Baqillani unusually allow the supreme imamate for any people.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r9.anchor: ولا اعتبار بضراز وأبي بكر الباقلاني حيث شذا فجوزاها في جميع الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r10.speaker: الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r10.claim: Shafi'i doctrine ranks a fallback imam Kinanite, then Ishmaelite, then Jurhumi if no qualified Qurayshi is available.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r10.anchor: وقال الشافعية : فإن لم يوجد قرشي أي مستجمع لشروط الإمامة اعتبر كون الإمام كنانيا

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r11.claim: Relying on ancestry while neglecting moral discipline shows poor judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r11.anchor: فالتقوى فالاتكال على النسب وترك النفس وهواها من ضعف الرأي وقلة العقل

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r12.claim: Noah's son was excluded for unrighteous conduct (11:46); the Prophet also called Salman one of the People of the House.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى لنوح عليه الصلاة والسلام في ابنه كنعان : ( إنه ليس من أهلك إنه عمل غير صالح )

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r13.claim: The Prophet said of Salman that he belonged to the People of the House.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r14.claim: A noble descendant should fear God and gain virtues sufficient even for someone without noble ancestry.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r14.anchor: فالحزم اللائق بالنسب أن يتقي الله ويكتسب منالخصال الحميدة ما لو كانت

ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r15.claim: Alusi criticizes descendants of Sufi lodge shaykhs who practice vice yet boast of fathers and scorn superior people.
ALUSI-FULL:v26p166/r15.anchor: وأكثر ما رأينا ذلك الافتخار البارد عند أولاد مشائخ الزوايا الصوفية فإنهم ارتكبوا كل رذيلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse came down about Thābit ibn Qays insulting a man who did not make room for him, calling him the son of a woman; the Prophet asked who had mentioned the woman, and Thābit admitted it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس، وقوله للرجل الذي لم يفسح له: ابن فلانة، يعيره بأمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
