BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r2.claim: The Prophet had Thābit look at the people; when Thābit saw white, red, and black faces, the Prophet said he was superior to them only through religion and piety.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r2.anchor: فقال: انظر في وجوه القوم فنظر فقال: ما رأيت يا ثابت؟ قال: رأيت أبيض وأحمر وأسود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r3.claim: The verse was revealed about Thābit, and the verse about making room in gatherings was revealed concerning the man who did not make room, Q 58:11.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس، وقوله للرجل الذي لم يفسح له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r4.claim: Muqātil says that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet sent Bilāl to call the adhān from the Kaʿba; ʿAttāb ibn Asīd lamented that his father had died before seeing the day, al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām called Bilāl a black crow, and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said God would make him change; Abū Sufyān kept silent for fear God in heaven would reveal his words.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا حتى علا ظهر الكعبة وأذن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r5.claim: Gabriel informed the Prophet of their remarks; he summoned and questioned them, they admitted, and the verse rebuked boasting of lineage and wealth and disparaging the poor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#2/r5.anchor: فأتى جبريل فأخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بما قالوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r1.claim: Male and female means Adam and Eve: people share equal lineage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r1.anchor: يعني آدم وحواء أي إنكم متساوون في النسب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r2.claim: Shuʿūb is the plural of shaʿb with an open shīn, the highest lineage group and root of tribes, such as Rabīʿa, Muḍar, Aws, and Khazraj; it is named for branching and gathering like the branches of a tree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r2.anchor: جمع شعب بفتح الشين، وهي رؤوس القبائل مثل ربيعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r3.claim: The root shaʿb is an antonym: it can mean to gather or to divide.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r3.anchor: والشعب من الأضداد يقال: شعب، أي: جمع، وشعب أي: فرق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r4.claim: Tribes rank below peoples, as Bakr within Rabīʿa and Tamīm within Muḍar.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r5.claim: Below tribes come ʿamāʾir, then abṭun, then afkhādh, then faṣāʾil and ʿashāʾir; examples include Shaybān and Dārim, Banū Ghālib and Luʾayy, and Banū Hāshim and Umayya; no lineage group after the ʿashīra is named.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r5.anchor: ودون القبائل العمائر، واحدتها عمارة، بفتح العين، وهم كشيبان من بكر، ودارم من تميم، ودون العمائر البطون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r6.claim: Another view says peoples are non-Arabs, tribes are Arabs, and asbāṭ are the tribes of the Children of Israel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r6.anchor: وقيل: الشعوب من العجم، والقبائل من العرب، والأسباط من بني إسرائيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r7.speaker: أبو روق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r7.claim: Abū Rawq says peoples are those who claim no ancestor and affiliate instead with towns and villages, while tribes are Arabs who trace descent through their fathers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p347#3/r7.anchor: وقال أبو روق: "الشعوب" الذين لا يعتزون إلى أحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r1.claim: Peoples and tribes are for mutual recognition across near and distant lineage, not boasting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r1.anchor: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب النسب وبعده، لا ليتفاخروا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r2.claim: The highest rank with God belongs to the person most mindful of Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r2.anchor: ثم أخبر أن أرفعهم منزلة عند الله أتقاهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r3.claim: Qatada says piety is the noblest generosity and wickedness the basest meanness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r3.anchor: قال قتادة في هذه الآية: إن أكرم الكرم التقوى، وألأم اللؤم الفجور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r4.claim: The Prophet says lineage-based honor is wealth, while true nobility is piety.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الحسب المال، والكرم التقوى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes worldly honor, which is wealth, from afterlife honor, which is piety.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كرم الدنيا الغنى، وكرم الآخرة التقوى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r6.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet said God had removed pre-Islamic tribal pride: people are either righteous and honored or wicked and lowly, then recited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r6.anchor: الناس رجلان بر تقي كريم على الله، وفاجر شقي هين على الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r7.claim: Asked who is most honored, the Prophet first answered the most pious, then named Joseph, and finally said the best Arabs in pre-Islamic times are best in Islam when they gain religious understanding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p348/r7.anchor: فخياركم في الجاهلية خياركم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r1.claim: People descend either from Adam and Eve or, distributively, from a father and mother; all are equal in this respect, so lineage is no basis for boasting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r1.anchor: من آدم وحواء عليهما السلام، أو خلقنا كل واحد منكم من أب وأم فالكل سواء في ذلك فلا وجه للتفاخر بالنسب

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r2.claim: The shared origin may also affirm brotherhood that restrains people from backbiting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تقريرا للأخوة المانعة عن الاغتياب

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r3.claim: A shaʿb is a large group tracing to one origin and contains tribes; tribes contain clans, clans subclans, subclans branches, and branches families. The cited examples progress from Khuzaima and Kinana to Quraysh, Qusay, Hashim, and Abbas.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r3.anchor: الشعب الجمع العظيم المنتسبون إلى أصل واحد وهو يجمع القبائل. والقبيلة تجمع العمائر. والعمارة تجمع البطون. والبطن تجمع الأفخاذ. والفخذ يجمع الفضائل

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r4.claim: Before the shaʿbs are subdivisions of non-Arabs, while Arab peoples are organized as tribes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r4.anchor: وقبل الشعوب بطون العجم والقبائل بطون العرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r5.claim: The purpose is mutual recognition, not pride in forefathers or tribal identity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r5.anchor: ليعرف بعضكم بعضا لا للتفاخر بالآباء والقبائل

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r6.claim: The phrase is read with assimilation as lataʿrafū, and also as litatārafū or lataʿrafū.

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r7.claim: The most honored before God is the most godfearing, since taqwā perfects souls and differentiates people; whoever seeks honor should seek it through taqwā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r7.anchor: فإن التقوى بها تكمل النفوس وتتفاضل بها الأشخاص، فمن أراد شرفا فليلتمسه منها

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever wants to be the most honored of people should fear God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r8.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام " من سره أن يكون أكرم الناس فليتق الله "

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r9.claim: A Prophetic report divides people into a pious believer, honored by God, and a wicked wretch, debased before God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13/r9.anchor:
وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام
" يا أيها الناس إنما الناس رجلان مؤمن تقي كريم على الله، وفاجر

BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13-14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13-14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13-14/r1.claim: God knows people and is aware of their inner realities.
BAYDAWI-FULL:49:13-14/r1.anchor: { إن الله عليم } بكم { خبير } ببواطنكم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r1.claim: The passage follows religious brotherhood and bans conduct prompted by self-admiration over ancestry; it overturns lineage-based privilege and directs believers to piety.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه الأخوة الدينية تذكيرا بالعاطف الموجب للإكرام , المانع من الانتقام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r2.claim: The address includes everyone, believers and others alike.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r3.claim: Human beings were created from nothing in their varied forms and lineages, from a male described as the locus of resolve and strength and a female as a place of weakness and repose; neither confers superiority.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r3.anchor: { من ذكر } هو المقصود بالعزم والقوة { وأنثى } هي موضع العضف والراحة , لا مزية لأحد منكم في ذلك على آخر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r4.claim: Peoples branch from a common origin; tribes lie beneath them, followed by subgroups, clans, branches, and families in a six-level lineage hierarchy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r4.anchor: جمع شعب بالفتح وهو الطيبقة الأولى من الطبقات الست

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r5.claim: He illustrates the lineage levels as Khuzayma (people), Kinana (tribe), Quraysh (subtribe), Qusayy (clan), Abd Manaf (branch), Hashim (family), and al-Abbas (household).
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r5.anchor: خزيمة شعب , وكنانة قبيلة , وقريش عمارة , وقصي بطن

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r6.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r6.claim: Al-Baghawi says no lineage group after the عشيرة is given a recognized collective name.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r6.anchor: قال البغوي : وليس بعد العشيرة حي يوصف به

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r7.claim: The verse names only peoples and tribes because these are the furthest lineage divisions people can readily recognize; the divisions below them are clearer still.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r7.anchor: واقتصر على الأولين لأنهما أقصى ما يسهل على الآدمي معرفته فما دونه أولى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r8.claim: Lineage divisions let people identify relatives and fulfill kinship duties, not recite pedigrees or boast.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r8.anchor: أي ليعرف الإنسان من يقاربه في النسب ليصل من رحمه ما يحق له , لا لتواصفوا وتفاخروا

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r9.claim: The prior verse's religious kinship implies that people should fear God in their relatives and those tied to them by family.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r9.anchor: كان التقدير : فتتقوا الله في أقاربكم وذوي أرحامكم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r10.claim: Against those who assume honor comes from lineage, the verse makes the most God-fearing the noblest before God, who alone grants honor and perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r10.anchor: مبطلا للتفاخر بالأنساب معللا لما أرشد إلى تقديره السياق مؤكدا لأجل ما عندهم من أن الكرم إنما هو بالنسب

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r11.claim: The Prophet says the best of people in the pre-Islamic era are the best in Islam when they gain understanding; the author explains this as a habit of understanding that leads to action.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r11.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( خياركم في الجاهلية خياركم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says the true jurist is one who acts on his knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p235#2/r12.anchor: كما قال الحسن رحمه الله : إنما الفقيه العامل بعلمه

DURR-FULL:v7p576#2/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p576#2/r14.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
DURR-FULL:v7p576#2/r14.claim: At the conquest, Bilāl called the prayer from the Kaaba; some objected to a Black enslaved man doing so and speculated God might change him, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v7p576#2/r14.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة قال: لما كان يوم الفتح رقي بلال فأذن على الكعبة فقال بعض الناس: هذا العبد الأسود

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r1.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r1.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the Prophet told Banū Bayāḍa to marry Abū Hind to one of their women; they objected to marrying their daughters to clients, and the verse was revealed specifically about Abū Hind, the Prophet's cupper.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r1.anchor: عن الزهري قال: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بني بياضة أن يزوجوا أبا هند امرأة منهم فقالوا

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r2.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r2.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet's instruction to marry Abū Hind and give him a wife, followed by the revelation of this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنكحوا أبا هند وانكحوا إليه

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r3.claim: Mujāhid says every child is created from the fluids of both a man and a woman, as the verse states.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: ما خلق الله الولد إلا من نطفة الرجل والمرأة جميعا

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r4.claim: ʿUmar says the verse in Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt is Meccan and addressed specifically to Arabs; he glosses the final criterion of honor as avoiding idolatry.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r4.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب أن هذه الآية في الحجرات {إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى} هي مكية

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r5.claim: ʿUmar interprets being most God-fearing as being most wary of associating partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r5.anchor: وقوله {إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم} قال: أتقاكم للشرك

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says shuʿūb are great tribes and qabāʾil are their subdivisions.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} قال: الشعوب القبائل العظام والقبائل البطون

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r7.claim: Another gloss from Ibn ʿAbbās calls shuʿūb large collectivities and qabāʾil the clans by which people recognize one another.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الشعوب الجماع والقبائل الأفخاذ التي يتعارفون بها

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says tribes are subdivisions while shuʿūb are large populations, such as Muḍar.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} قال: القبائل الأفخاذ والشعوب الجمهور مثل مضر

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r9.claim: Qatāda defines a shuʿb as distant ancestry and a qabīla as the nearer lineage expressed by saying someone is from a particular clan.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r9.anchor: عن قتادة {وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل} قال: الشعب هو النسب البعيد والقبائل كما سمعته يقول

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r10.claim: Mujāhid says shuʿūb are distant lineage and qabāʾil are nearer divisions; God made them so people could identify one another's descent.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد {وجعلناكم شعوبا} قال: النسب البعيد {وقبائل} قال: دون ذلك جعلنا هذا لتعرفوا فلان بن فلان

DURR-FULL:v7p578/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r11.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk calls qabāʾil the leading clans and shuʿūb the lineages, subdivisions, and branches.
DURR-FULL:v7p578/r11.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: القبائل رؤوس القبائل والشعوب الفصائل والأفخاذ

DURR-FULL:v7p579/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r1.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r1.claim: At the conquest sermon, the Prophet says God removed pre-Islamic shame and pride in ancestry: people are either righteous and honored or wicked and abased, and all descend from Adam, created from soil.
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طاف يوم الفتح على راحلته يستلم الأركان

DURR-FULL:v7p579/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r2.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r2.claim: In the farewell sermon, the Prophet declares that all people have one Lord and father; neither Arab nor non-Arab, Black nor red has precedence except through piety, and witnesses must convey the message.
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وسط أيام التشريق خطبة الوداع

DURR-FULL:v7p579/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r3.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r3.claim: The Prophet says God removed pre-Islamic pride in ancestry, all people descend from Adam and Eve, and a suitor whose religion and trustworthiness are acceptable should be allowed to marry.
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن الله أذهب نخوة الجاهلية وتكبرها بآبائها

DURR-FULL:v7p579/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r4.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r4.claim: The Prophet says all are children of Adam and lineage gives no superiority; God will not ask about rank or ancestry on Judgment Day, but honor belongs to the most pious.
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r4.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن أنسابكم هذه ليست بمسيئة على أحد

DURR-FULL:v7p579/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r5.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r5.claim: A divine address on Judgment Day rebukes people for neglecting God's charge while elevating their genealogies.
DURR-FULL:v7p579/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله يقول يوم القيامة أمرتكم فضيعتم ما عهدت إليكم ورفعتم أنسابكم

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r1.claim: A prophetic saying adds that the best people in the pre-Islamic era are the best in Islam when they gain religious understanding.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r1.anchor: خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r2.claim: The Prophet tells Abū Dharr that neither a red nor a Black person is better than him unless superior in piety.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: أنظر فإنك لست بخير من أحمر ولا أسود إلا أن تفضله بتقوى

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās observes that people do not seem to practice this verse when one boasts of being more noble; no one is nobler than another except by piety.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: لا أرى أحدا يعمل بهذه الآية {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى}

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God has defined nobility as piety and lineage as excellence of character.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: ما تعدون الكرم وقد بين الله الكرم وأكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r5.claim: Asked who is best, the Prophet names those most versed in recitation, most God-fearing, most active in commanding right and forbidding wrong, and closest in maintaining kinship.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r5.anchor: عن درة بنت أبي لهب قالت: قام رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو على المنبر فقال: يا رسول الله أي الناس خير

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r6.claim: A report graded sound by al-Tirmidhī states that social standing is wealth and true nobility is piety.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r6.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: الحسب المال والكرم التقوى

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet was never impressed by worldly things or by any person except one marked by piety.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r7.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: ما أعجب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيء من الدنيا ولا أعجبه أحد قط إلا ذو تقوى

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says God makes everything fear a person who fears Him, while making the person who does not fear Him afraid of everything.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r8.anchor: عن واثلة بن الأسقع رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من اتقى الله أهاب الله منه كل شيء

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r9.claim: The Prophet calls modesty an adornment, piety nobility, patience the best mount, and waiting for God's relief an act of worship.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r9.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: الحياء زينة والتقى كرم وخير المركب الصبر

DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r10.claim: The Prophet says that when God wills good for someone, He places self-sufficiency within and piety in the heart; when He wills evil, poverty stays before the person's eyes.
DURR-FULL:v7p580#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا أراد الله بعبده خيرا جعل غناه في نفسه وتقاه في قلبه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “peoples” are large groups, while tribes are their subdivisions through which people recognize one another.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : الشعوب الجماع ، والقبائل الافخاذ التي يتعارفون بها .

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet’s sermon at the conquest of Mecca: God removed pre-Islamic pride in ancestry; people are either pious and noble to God or wicked and lowly, and the most honored are the most pious.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3306#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : طاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة على ناقته القصواء

IBNHIBBAN:3828/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:3828/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNHIBBAN:3828/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet said God had removed pre-Islamic tribal pride, and that people are either pious and honored or wicked and low; he recited this verse.
IBNHIBBAN:3828/r1.anchor: عن بن عمر قال: طاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على راحلته القصواء يوم الفتح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r1.claim: From a male and a female may mean Adam and Eve, so all people descend from them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r1.anchor: من ذكر وأنثى يحتمل أن يريد آدم وحواء. فكأنه قال: إنا خلقنا جميعكم من آدم وحواء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the words denote the two sexes: each person is created from the male’s and female’s fluid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد الذكر والأنثى اسم الجنس. فكأنه قال: إنا خلقنا كل واحد منكم من ماء ذكر وماء أنثى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r3.claim: The verse aims to establish equality among people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r3.anchor: وقصد هذه الآية التسوية بين الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r4.claim: Peoples and tribes are made so people can recognize one another, not boast or seek to outrank one another; honor instead comes through piety.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r4.anchor: أي لئلا تفاخروا ويريد بعضكم أن يكون أكرم من بعض. فإن الطريق إلى الكرم غير هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakra reports that when the Prophet was asked who the best people are, he answered: the one whose life is long and deeds are good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r5.anchor: وروى أبو بكرة: قيل يا رسول الله: من خير الناس؟ قال: «من طال عمره وحسن عمله»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r6.claim: Another report says the best people most command right, forbid wrong, maintain kinship ties, and fear God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r6.anchor: وفي حديث آخر من خير الناس؟ قال: «آمرهم بالمعروف. وأنهاهم عن المنكر. وأوصلهم للرحم وأتقاهم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r7.speaker: الزهراوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r7.claim: Al-Zahrawi gives as the occasion the anger of al-Harith ibn Hisham and ʿAttab ibn Asid when Bilal called the prayer from the Kaʿba at the conquest of Mecca.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r7.anchor: وحكى الزهراوي أن سبب هذه الآية غضب الحارث بن هشام وعتاب بن أسيد حين أذن بلال يوم فتح مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r8.speaker: الثعلبي عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r8.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the occasion was Thabit ibn Qays insulting a man who failed to make room near the Prophet; the Prophet rebuked him, saying distinction is only by religion and piety, and the verse and command to make room followed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r8.anchor: وحكى الثعلبي عن ابن عباس أن سببها قول ثابت بن قيس لرجل لم يفسح عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا ابن فلانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r9.claim: The genealogical hierarchy runs from shuʿub, the largest lineage group, to tribe, ʿimara, clan, subclan, then the nearest family and lineage group.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r9.anchor: والشعوب: جمع شعب وهو أعظم ما يوجد من جماعات الناس مرتبطا بنسب واحد، ويتلوه القبيلة، ثم العمارة، ثم البطن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r10.claim: Examples are Mudar, Rabiʿa, and Himyar as shuʿub; Qays, Tamim, Madhhij, and Murad as tribes; Quraysh, Muharib, and Sulaym as ʿimara; the Banu groups then exemplify smaller ranks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r10.anchor: فمضر وربيعة وحمير شعوب، وقيس وتميم ومذحج ومراد، قبائل مشبهة بقبائل الرأس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r11.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p152#2/r11.claim: Ibn Jubayr says shuʿub are the subclans.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported to define shuʿub as clans, a view contrary to the consensus of linguists cited by Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r1.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس الشعوب: البطون، وهذا غير ما تمالأ عليه اللغويون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r2.speaker: الثعلبي وقيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r2.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi and another reported view say shuʿub are non-Arabs, tribes are Arabs, and asbat are the Israelites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r2.anchor: قال الثعلبي، وقيل: الشعوب في العجم والقبائل في العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r3.claim: The Hamdan group called al-Shaʿbi is a subclan named al-Shaʿb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r3.anchor: وأما الشعب الذي هو في همدان الذي ينسب إليه الشعبي فهو بطن يقال له الشعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r4.claim: The label Shuʿubiyya for non-Arabs derives from shuʿub because their detailed genealogies were hidden and they were identified by broad peoples; this is a changed nisba and, among other explanations, the best one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r4.anchor: فعرفوا بشعوبهم وهي أعم ما يعبر به عن جماعتهم، ويقال لهم الشعوبية بفتح الشين، وهذا من تغيير النسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas read لتعرفوا أن; Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers a purpose-lām interpretation awkward, an imperative-lām interpretation better, and also allows an omitted object meaning the truth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r6.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن عباس: «لتعرفوا أن» ، على وزن تفعلوا بكسر العين وفتح الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r7.claim: With purpose lām, people are equal as creatures so they may know one another and the truths; honor comes from piety and sound hearts. He judges the imperative lām better for Ibn ʿAbbas’s reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون لام الأمر، وهو أجود في المعنى، ويحتمل أن يكون المفعول محذوفا تقديره: الحق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud read لتعارفوا بينكم وخيركم عند الله أتقاكم.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: «لتعارفوا بينكم وخيركم عند الله أتقاكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r9.claim: The Prophet said that whoever wants to be the most honored among people should fear God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r9.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «من سره أن يكون أكرم الناس، فليتق الله»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r10.claim: God is fully aware of the pious person who deserves the rank of honor through faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p153/r10.anchor: إن الله عليم خبير أي بالمتقي الذي يستحق رتبة الكرم في الإيمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r1.claim: One occasion says the verse concerned Thabit ibn Qays, who insulted a man for not making room by calling him the son of a certain woman; Ibn Abbas's report is cited under 49:11.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r1.anchor: نزلت في ثابت بن قيس وقوله في الرجل الذي لم يفسح له أنت ابن فلانة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r2.claim: Muqatil says the verse followed the conquest of Mecca: Bilal called the prayer from the Kaaba, provoking remarks from ʿAttab, al-Harith, Suhayl, and Abu Sufyan about his race and status.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه لما كان يوم الفتح أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا فصعد على ظهر الكعبة فأذن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r3.speaker: يزيد بن شجرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r3.claim: Yazid ibn Shajara says the verse followed the Prophet's visit to a sick black servant and his personally washing, shrouding, and burying him after death.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r3.anchor: أن عبدا أسود مرض فعاده رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم قبض فتولى غسله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r4.claim: The man and woman are Adam and Eve; people are equal in lineage, so the verse rebukes boasting about ancestry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r4.anchor: فأما المراد بالذكر والأنثى فآدم وحواء والمعنى إنكم تتساوون في النسب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r5.speaker: الجمهور من المفسرين وأهل اللغة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r5.claim: Most exegetes and linguists say shuʿub are large groups such as Mudar and Rabiʿa, while qabaʾil are smaller clans such as Bakr and Tamim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r5.anchor: فأما الشعوب فهي جمع شعب وهو الحي العظيم مثل مضر وربيعة والقبائل دونها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r6.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through ʿAtaʾ identifies shuʿub as clients and qabaʾil as Arabs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r6.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال يريد بالشعوب الموالي وبالقبائل العرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r7.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r7.claim: Abu Razin says shuʿub are mountain people who claim no affiliation, while qabaʾil are Arab tribes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r7.anchor: وقال أبو رزين الشعوب أهل الجبال الذين لا يعتزون لأحد والقبائل قبائل العرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r8.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r8.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi also reports the inverse arrangement: qabaʾil are roots and shuʿub are branches growing from them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p473/r8.anchor: وقد قيل إن القبائل هي الأصول والشعوب هي البطون التي تتشعب منها وهذا ضد القول الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r1.claim: The purpose is for people to recognize one another by closeness and distance of kinship, not to boast; the most honored before God is the most pious.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r1.anchor: أي ليعرف بعضكم بعضا في قرب النسب وبعده قال الزجاج المعنى جعلناكم كذلك لتعارفوا لا لتفاخروا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب وابن عباس والضحاك وابن يعمر وأبان عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r2.claim: These readers read li-taʿrafu with a silent ʿayn, kasra on the rāʾ, and no alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r2.anchor: قرأ أبي بن كعب وابن عباس والضحاك وابن يعمر وأبان عن عاصم لتعرفوا باسكان العين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r3.speaker: مجاهد وأبو المتوكل وابن محيصن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r3.claim: Mujahid, Abu al-Mutawakkil, and Ibn Muhaysin read the form with one doubled tāʾ, an alif, and an ungeminated rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r3.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وأبو المتوكل وابن محيصن لتعارفوا بتاء واحدة مشددة وبألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r4.speaker: أبو نهيك والأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r4.claim: Abu Nuhayk and al-Aʿmash read litaʿarra fu with two tāʾs, a doubled rāʾ, and no alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو نهيك والأعمش لتتعرفوا بتاءين مفتوحة الراء وبتشديدها من غير ألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي ومجاهد وأبو الجوزاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r5.claim: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Mujahid, and Abu al-Jawzaʾ read the hamza in an akramakum with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي ومجاهد وأبو الجوزاء أن بفتح الهمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ says opening the hamza means “so you may know that the most honored is the most pious”; though li-taʿrifu might be expected, li-taʿarafu is also permissible in that sense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p474/r6.anchor: قال الفراء من فتح أن فكأنه قال لتعارفوا أن الكريم التقي ولو كان كذلك لكانت لتعرفوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r1.claim: Humanity descends from one soul, Adam, and his spouse Eve, whom God made from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r1.anchor: خلقهم من نفس واحدة، وجعل منها زوجها، وهما آدم وحواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r2.claim: Clans or peoples (shuʿūb) are broader than tribes (qabāʾil); further subdivisions include lineages, families, clans, and branches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r2.anchor: وهي أعم من القبائل، وبعد القبائل مراتب أخر كالفصائل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r3.claim: An alternative view takes shuʿūb as subdivisions of non-Arabs and qabāʾil as subdivisions of Arabs, like the Israelite tribes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r3.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالشعوب بطون العجم، وبالقبائل بطون العرب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r4.claim: All people are equal in their earthly descent from Adam and Eve; they differ in religious merit through obeying God and following His Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r4.anchor: فجميع الناس في الشرف بالنسبة الطينية إلى آدم وحواء سواء، وإنما يتفاضلون بالأمور الدينية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r5.claim: The purpose of peoples and tribes is that people recognize one another by lineage; the point follows the prohibitions on backbiting and looking down on others and underscores shared humanity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r5.anchor: منبها على تساويهم في البشرية: {يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase by identifying someone through a family name and tribe, as in saying whose son he is and where he belongs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {لتعارفوا} ، كما يقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r7.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r7.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says the Himyar identified themselves by their regions, while the Arabs of the Hijaz identified themselves by their tribes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r7.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري: كانت حمير ينتسبون إلى مخاليفها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet’s advice to learn enough genealogy to maintain kinship, which brings affection among relatives, increases wealth, and lengthens life; al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb and says it is known only by this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p385/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "تعلموا من أنسابكم ما تصلون به أرحامكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r1.claim: People’s standing with God depends on piety, not ancestry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r1.anchor: إنما تتفاضلون عند الله بالتقوى لا بالأحساب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet named the most God-fearing as most noble; when asked about Arab lineages, he said the best in pre-Islamic times are best in Islam if they gain understanding, and he also named Joseph’s noble prophetic ancestry.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الناس أكرم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet said God looks at people’s hearts and deeds, not their appearance or wealth; Muslim and Ibn Majah transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة (7) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r4.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr that no red or black person is better than him except through greater piety; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: "انظر، فإنك لست بخير من أحمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r5.speaker: محمد بن حبيب بن خراش العصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Habib reports from his father that the Prophet said Muslims are brothers and no one has merit over another except through piety.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r5.anchor: سمعت محمد بن حبيب بن خراش العصري، يحدث عن أبيه: أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول (13) : المسلمون إخوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r6.speaker: حذيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r6.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet said all are children of Adam, who was created from dust, and warned people to stop boasting of their forefathers or become lower before God than dung beetles.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p386/r6.anchor: عن حذيفة (4) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كلكم بنو آدم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r1.speaker: البزار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r1.claim: Al-Bazzar says the report from Hudhayfa is known only through this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r1.anchor: ثم قال: لا نعرفه عن حذيفة إلا من هذا الوجه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r2.claim: Ibn Umar reports that during the conquest of Mecca the Prophet preached from his camel, saying God had removed pre-Islamic pride in ancestry: people are either pious and honored by God or wicked and lowly; he recited this verse. Ibn Kathir notes Abd ibn Humayd also transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: طاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة على ناقته القصواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r3.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r3.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that lineages are no ground for disparagement: all people descend from Adam, and only religion and piety confer merit; abusive, miserly, obscene behavior is blameworthy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r3.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن أنسابكم هذه ليست بمسبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r4.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir’s wording of the report says all people descend from Adam and Eve, are alike as an unfilled small measure, and will be judged for piety rather than ancestry; Ibn Kathir says this route is absent from the six canonical collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r4.anchor: ولفظه: "الناس لآدم وحواء، طف الصاع لم يملئوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r5.speaker: درة بنت أبي لهب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r5.claim: Durrah bint Abi Lahab reports that the Prophet named the best people as those who recite most, fear God, command right, forbid wrong, and maintain kinship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p387/r5.anchor: عن درة بنت أبي لهب قالت: قام رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو على المنبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r1.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet admired nothing in worldly life and no person except one possessing piety; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: ما أعجب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيء من الدنيا، ولا أعجبه أحد قط

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r2.claim: God knows people and their affairs; He guides, misguides, shows mercy, punishes, and grants preference by His wisdom and knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r2.anchor: عليم بكم، خبير بأموركم، فيهدي من يشاء، ويضل من يشاء، ويرحم من يشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r3.claim: Some scholars infer from this verse and the cited reports that marriage compatibility is not a condition beyond religion; other scholars rely on different evidence discussed in legal works.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r3.anchor: من ذهب من العلماء إلى أن الكفاءة في النكاح لا تشترط، ولا يشترط سوى الدين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r4.claim: Al-Tabarani reports that when a man from Banu Hashim claimed to be closest to the Prophet, Abd al-Rahman answered that another person was more entitled to him, while the claimant had kinship to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p388/r4.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن أنه سمع رجلا من بني هاشم يقول: أنا أولى الناس برسول الله.

JISHUMI:v9p6517/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة ومجاهد وغيرهم
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid, and others report that Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt is Medinan.
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r1.anchor: مدنية فيما روي عن الحسن، وقتادة، وعكرمة، ومجاهد وغيرهم

JISHUMI:v9p6517/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the sūra is Medinan except for this verse, and counts it as eighteen verses.
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنها مدنية، إلا قوله: (ياأيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى)، وهي ثماني عشرة آية

JISHUMI:v9p6517/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r3.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet, transmitted by Ubayy b. Kaʿb, promises the reciter ten good deeds for each person who obeys God and each who disobeys Him.
JISHUMI:v9p6517/r3.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: من قرأ سورة (الحجرات)، أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات

JISHUMI:v9p6533/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r6.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says shuʿūb are larger groupings than tribes.
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r6.anchor: والشعوب: قال الفراء: أكثر من القبائل

JISHUMI:v9p6533/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r7.speaker: الليث
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r7.claim: Al-Layth defines a shaʿb as a grouping that branches into Arab tribes.
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r7.anchor: وقال الليث: الشعب ما يتشعب من قبائل العرب

JISHUMI:v9p6533/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r8.claim: A shaʿūbī belittles Arabs and denies their superiority, interpreting the verse's shuʿūb as non-Arabs and qabāʾil as Arabs.
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r8.anchor: والشعوبي: الذي يصغر شأن العرب، ولا يرى لهم فضلا على غيرهم سموا بذلك لأنهم تأولوا (وجعلناكم شعوبا)

JISHUMI:v9p6533/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says shuʿūb means non-Arabs.

JISHUMI:v9p6533/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r10.claim: The word comes from branching and extensive division of lineage; shaʿabahu can mean joining or dividing, while shaʿaba amrahu means dispersing it, and the root can also describe repairing a division.
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r10.anchor: وأصل الشعوب من التشعب وهو كثرة تفرقهم في النسب، يقال: شغبته: جمعته، وشعبته: فرقته، وهو من الأضداد

JISHUMI:v9p6533/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r11.speaker: عائشة
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r11.claim: In a report describing Abū Bakr, ʿĀʾisha uses the expression for repairing the community's division after its unity fractured; the same root can describe repairing broken vessels.
JISHUMI:v9p6533/r11.anchor: ومنه حديث عائشة في صفة أبيها يرأب شعبها، أي: شعب الأمة لما افترقت كلمتها بينها

JISHUMI:v9p6534/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6534/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v9p6534/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that this verse was revealed after Thābit b. Qays insulted a man by invoking his mother; when the Prophet asked who had mentioned her, Thābit confessed, and the Prophet told him to look at the faces of the people. Thābit saw white, black, and red faces, and was told that he surpassed them only by religion.
JISHUMI:v9p6534/r7.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v9p6540/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r1.claim: All people descend from Adam and Eve.

JISHUMI:v9p6540/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r2.claim: Human lineage existed before religious law.
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r2.anchor: ومنها: أن النسب كان ثابتا قبل الشرع

JISHUMI:v9p6540/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r3.claim: The purpose of peoples and tribes is mutual recognition.

JISHUMI:v9p6540/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r4.claim: Merit comes through piety, not ancestry.
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r4.anchor: ومنها: أن الفضل بالتقوى لا بالأنساب

JISHUMI:v9p6540/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r5.claim: A report says a caller at the Resurrection will summon only the pious to stand, since God made piety the true lineage.
JISHUMI:v9p6540/r5.anchor: وفي الخبر: أن مناديا ينادي يوم القيامة: إني جعلت لكم نسبا وجعلتم لأنفسكم نسبا، (إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم)، ليقم المتقون، فلا يقوم إلا من كان كذلك

TIRMIDHI:3270/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3270/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
TIRMIDHI:3270/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's conquest-of-Mecca sermon rejecting ancestral arrogance: people rank by piety, all descend from Adam, created from dust. Al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb.
TIRMIDHI:3270/r1.anchor: عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَطَبَ النَّاسَ يَوْمَ فَتْحِ مَكَّةَ

TIRMIDHI:3270/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3270/r2.speaker: author
TIRMIDHI:3270/r2.claim: Tirmidhi notes Yahya ibn Ma'in and others weakened Abdullah ibn Ja'far, the route is gharīb, and reports also come from Abu Hurayra and Ibn Abbas.
TIRMIDHI:3270/r2.anchor: وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ يُضَعَّفُ ضَعَّفَهُ يَحْيَى بْنُ مَعِينٍ وَغَيْرُهُ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r1.claim: The man and woman are Adam and Eve.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r1.anchor: من ذكر وأنثى } من آدم وحواء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r2.claim: Alternatively every person is from a father and mother, so all have equal origins and none can claim superiority by lineage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r2.anchor: خلقنا كل واحد منكم من أب وأم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r3.claim: Arab genealogy has six levels, shaʿb, tribe, ʿimara, batn, fakhidh, and family, illustrated by Khuzayma, Kinana, Quraysh, Qusay, Hashim, and al-Abbas.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r3.anchor: الطبقة الأولى من الطبقات الست التي عليها العرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r4.claim: Variants include لتتعارفوا with assimilation, لتعارفوا, لِتَعرفوا, and لتتعرفوا; one means learning how people are related.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r5.claim: The purpose of tribes and clans is for people to identify one another's ancestry, not to claim other fathers or boast in lineage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r5.anchor: أن الحكمة التي من أجلها رتبكم على شعوب وقبائل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r6.claim: Piety, not ancestry, is the trait by which a person gains honor and dignity with God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r6.anchor: الخصلة التي بها يفضل الإنسان غيره ويكتسب الشرف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r7.claim: A variant reads أن with fatḥa, explaining that the most honored before God are the most pious, not the best-born.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r7.anchor: وقرىء : ( أن ) بالفتح ، كأنه قيل : لم لا يتفاخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r8.claim: At Mecca's conquest, the Prophet said God removed pagan arrogance and people are either pious believers honored by God or wicked, wretched people low in His sight, then recited the verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r8.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1079 ) أنه طاف يوم فتح مكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r9.claim: The Prophet said whoever wants to be the most honored of people should fear God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r9.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام : ( 1080 ) ( من سره أن يكون أكرم الناس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes worldly nobility, which is wealth, from next-world nobility, which is piety.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r10.anchor: كرم الدنيا الغني ، وكرم الآخرة التقوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r11.speaker: يزيد بن شجرة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r11.claim: Yazid ibn Shajara reports that the Prophet bought a Black boy who stipulated he not be kept from the five prayers behind him; after the boy fell ill and died, the Prophet visited, washed, and buried him, deeply affecting the Emigrants and Helpers, and the verse was revealed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p377#2/r11.anchor: وعو يزيد بن شجرة : ( 1081 ) مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سوق المدينة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.claim: The verse forbids boasting about ancestry and establishes equality through common descent from Adam and Eve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r1.anchor: قصد بهذه الآية . النهي عن التفاخر بالأنساب , وبين التساوي فيها بأن خلقهم من ذكر وأنثى يعني آدم وحواء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.claim: Peoples and tribes exist for mutual recognition, not boasting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r2.anchor: فبين أن الشعوب والقبائل للتعارف لا للافتخار ، وفيها ثلاثة أوجه :

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say peoples are more distant lineages and tribes closer ones; the cited poem and tribal branching support the distinction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r3.anchor: أحدها : أن الشعوب النسب الأبعد والقبائل النسب الأقرب , قاله مجاهد , وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.claim: A second view makes peoples the Arabs of Yemen from Qahtan, and tribes Rabi'a, Mudar, and the rest of Adnan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : أن الشعوب عرب اليمن من قحطان ، والقبيلة ربيعة ومضر وسائر عدنان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.claim: A third view takes peoples as subdivisions of non-Arabs and tribes as subdivisions of Arabs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r5.anchor: الثالث : أن الشعوب بطون العجم , والقبائل بطون العرب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.claim: Mawardi suggests peoples are linked to regions and valleys, while tribes share ancestry; a poem illustrates scattered peoples.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أن الشعوب هم المضافون إلى النواحي والشعاب , والقبائل هم المشتركون في الأنساب , قال الشاعر : وتفرقوا شعبا فكل جزيرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r7.claim: Shuʿub with fatḥa is the plural of shaʿb; shaʿb with kasra means road and its plural is shiʿab, so the vowel distinction signals different meanings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r7.anchor: والشعوب جمع شعب بفتح الشين , والشعب بكسر الشين هو الطريق وجمعه شعاب , فكان اختلاف الجمعين مع اتفاق اللفظين تنبيها على اختلاف المعنيين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r8.claim: The most excellent are those most pious; nobility comes through deeds and piety, not ancestry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p335#2/r8.anchor: إن أفضلكم , والكرم بالعمل والتقوى لا بالنسب .

MUJAHID:v2p608/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p608/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p608/r1.claim: Mujahid defines shuʿūb as distant lineages and tribes as lineages nearer than those.
MUJAHID:v2p608/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال الشعوب النسب البعيد والقبائل دون ذلك

MUJAHID:v2p608/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p608/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p608/r2.claim: God made people into lineages so they could identify one another by ancestry, as in knowing whose son someone is and where he comes from.
MUJAHID:v2p608/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال الشعوب النسب البعيد والقبائل دون ذلك يقول جعلنا هذا لتعرفوا فلان بن فلان من كذا وكذا

MUQATIL:49:13/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r1.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed concerning Bilal; he also reports that it was said to concern Salman al-Farisi and four Quraysh men: Attab, al-Harith, Suhayl, and Abu Sufyan.
MUQATIL:49:13/r1.anchor: نزلت في بلال المؤذن، وقالوا: في سلمان الفارسي، وفي أربعة نفر من قريش، في عتاب بن أسيد بن أبي العيص

MUQATIL:49:13/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r2.claim: After the conquest of Mecca, Muhammad ordered Bilal to call the prayer from the Kaaba roof in order to humble the polytheists.
MUQATIL:49:13/r2.anchor: لما فتح مكة أمر بلالا فصعد ظهر الكعبة وأذن، وأراد أن يذل المشركين بذلك

MUQATIL:49:13/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r3.claim: Attab thanked God his father died before this day; al-Harith mocked Bilal as a black crow and wondered why Muhammad chose him.
MUQATIL:49:13/r3.anchor: قال عتاب بن أسيد: الحمد لله الذي قبض أسيد قبل هذا اليوم، وقال الحارث بن هشام: عجبت لهذا العبد الحبشي

MUQATIL:49:13/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r4.claim: Suhayl said God would change anything He disliked; Abu Sufyan stayed silent, fearing heaven and earth would testify against him.
MUQATIL:49:13/r4.anchor: وقال سهيل بن عمرو: إن يكره الله شيئا يغيره، وقال أبو سفيان: أمأ أنا فلا أقول

MUQATIL:49:13/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r5.claim: Gabriel informed Muhammad of their remarks; Muhammad asked each man what he had said, and affirmed each man's account as true.
MUQATIL:49:13/r5.anchor: فنزل جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبره بقوله

MUQATIL:49:13/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r6.claim: People are Adam and Eve's descendants; peoples are tribal heads such as Rabi ah, Mudar, Tamim, and Azd, while tribes are clans such as Banu Sad, Amir, and Qays, enabling recognition of lineage.
MUQATIL:49:13/r6.anchor: يعني رءوس القبائل ربيعة ومضر وبنو تميم والأزد

MUQATIL:49:13/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:49:13/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:49:13/r7.claim: Muqatil identifies Bilal as the most honored and most God-fearing person in the verse.
MUQATIL:49:13/r7.anchor: { إن أكرمكم } يعني بلالا { عند الله أتقاكم إن الله عليم خبير } [آية: 13] يعني أن أتقاكم بلال.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r1.claim: The pair may be Adam and Eve, or each person may be understood as descended from a father and mother; since all share equal descent, lineage is no ground for pride.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r1.anchor: من آدم وحواء أو كل واحد منكم من اب وام فما منكم من أحد الا وهو يدلى بمثل ما يدلى به الاخر سواء بسواء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r2.claim: The six Arab lineage ranks are shaʿb, tribe, ʿimāra, clan, branch and family: a shaʿb gathers tribes, which gather the succeeding ranks; the example runs from Khuzayma through Kināna, Quraysh, Quṣayy and Hāshim to al-ʿAbbās.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r2.anchor: الشعب الطبقة الاولى من الطبقات الست التى عليها العرب وهى الشعب والقبيلة والعمارة والبطن والفخذ والفصيلة فالشعب يجمع القبائل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r3.claim: They are called shuʿūb because tribes branch out from them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r3.anchor: وسمت الشعوب لان القبائل تشعبت منها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r4.claim: The purpose of lineage ranks is to recognize one another's ancestry, not to boast, claim superiority through forebears, or attribute oneself to someone other than one's father.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r4.anchor: اى انما رتبكم على شعوب وقبائل ليعرف بعضكم نسب بعض فلا يعترى إلى غير آبائه لا ان تتفاخروا بالآباء والاجداد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r5.claim: Piety, not ancestry, is the quality by which a person earns honor and nobility before Allah.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r5.anchor: ثم بين الخصلة التي يفضل بها الانسان غيره ويكتسب الشرف والكرم عند الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says whoever wants to be the most honored should fear Allah; worldly honor is wealth, while otherworldly honor is piety.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r6.anchor: في الحديث من سره ان يكون اكرم الناس فليتق الله عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما كرم الدنيا الغنى وكرم الاخرة التقوى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r7.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet praised Allah and said humanity comprises a pious believer, noble before Allah, and a wicked sinner, low before Him, then recited the verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r7.anchor: وروى انه صلى الله عليه وسلم طاف يوم فتح مكه فحمد الله واثنى عليه ثم قال الحمد لله الذى اذهب عنكم غيبة الجاهلية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r8.speaker: يزيد ابن شجرة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r8.claim: Yazīd ibn Shajara reports that the Prophet saw a black enslaved boy in Medina's market who stipulated that his buyer let him pray the five prayers behind the Prophet; after the boy died, people remarked on the matter at his burial and the verse was revealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r8.anchor: وعن يزيد ابن شجرة مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سوق المدينة فرأى غلاما اسود يقول من اشترانى فعلى شرط

NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r9.claim: Allah knows the nobility and piety of hearts and is aware of people's innermost inclinations and desires.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p167#2/r9.anchor: ﴿ إن الله عليم ﴾ كرم القلوب وتقواها

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r1.claim: “A male and a female” means Adam and Eve.

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r2.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the verse was revealed specifically about Abū Hind: the Prophet ordered Banū Bayāḍa to marry him to a woman of their group, and they objected to marrying daughters to clients; Abū Dāwūd records the report in al-Marāsīl.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r2.anchor: قال الزهري: نزلت في أبي هند خاصة

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r3.claim: Another occasion says the verse concerned Thābit ibn Qays, who insulted a man not making room by calling him the son of a woman; the Prophet said no one excels others except through piety.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنها نزلت في ثابت بن قيس بن شماس. وقوله في الرجل الذي لم يتفسح له

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r4.claim: In the Thābit report, the Prophet says no one excels others except through piety; 58:11 was revealed about the man who was not given room.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r4.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:«انظر في وجوه القوم

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at the conquest of Mecca Bilāl called the prayer from the Kaʿba; ʿAttāb, al-Ḥārith, and Suhayl disparaged him, while Abū Sufyān feared God would inform the Prophet; Gabriel did so, the men admitted their remarks, and the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا حتى علا على ظهر الكعبة

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r6.claim: The verse rebukes boasting in ancestry, competing in wealth, and looking down on the poor: the criterion is piety, since everyone descends from Adam and Eve.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13/r6.anchor: زجرهم عن التفاخر بالأنساب، والتكاثر بالأموال، والازدراء بالفقراء

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying God removed jāhiliyya arrogance over ancestors: people are either righteous and honored by God or wicked and lowly; all descend from Adam, whom God created from dust.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r1.anchor: يأيها الناس إن الله قد أذهب عنكم عيبة الجاهلية وتعاظمها بآبائها

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معين
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r2.claim: The preceding Ibn ʿUmar report is transmitted through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, father of ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī; Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn and others graded it weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r2.anchor: خرجه من حديث عبد الله بن جعفر والد علي بن المديني وهو ضعيف، ضعفه يحيى بن معين وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from Abū Naḍra the Prophet’s sermon at Minā during the middle days of Tashrīq: one Lord and father, no Arab/non-Arab or color group excels another except by piety, and witnesses should tell those absent.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي نضرة قال: حدثني أو حدثنا من شهد

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r4.claim: Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī reports that God looks at hearts rather than status, ancestry, bodies, or wealth; all are Adam’s children, and the most pious are dearest to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r4.anchor: وفيه عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r5.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r5.claim: A poem attributed to ʿAlī says humans are equal through Adam and Eve, clay and water confer no honor, and worth lies in knowledge, guidance, and what a person does well rather than ignorance or ancestry.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r5.anchor: ولعلي رضي الله عنه في هذا المعنى وهو مشهور من شعره

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r6.claim: The creation from male and female is also stated at the beginning of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ; God could have created without a pair, as Adam, without a male, as Jesus, or without a female, as Eve.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r6.anchor: وكذلك في أول سورة «النساء». ولو شاء لخلقه دونهما كخلقه لآدم

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī notes that Eve was created from Adam’s rib, perhaps representing creation from one parent alone; divine power to create in other ways did not make those possibilities actual.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r7.anchor: وقد جاء أن آدم خلق الله منه حواء من ضلع انتزعها من أضلاعه فلعله هذا القسم قاله ابن العربي

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r8.claim: God made people into lineages, in-law relations, tribes, and peoples so that they could recognize and connect with one another, according to His determined wisdom.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r8.anchor: خلق الله الخلق بين الذكر والأنثى أنسابا وأصهارا وقبائل وشعوبا، وخلق لهم منها التعارف

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r9.claim: Denying someone’s actual lineage can incur the legal penalty for slander, including falsely calling an Arab non-Arab or vice versa.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#2/r9.anchor: فإذا نفاه رجل عنه استوجب الحد بقذفه مثل أن ينفيه عن رهطه وحسبه

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r1.claim: An earlier view held that a fetus comes only from the man’s fluid; the preceding quotations are cited to argue creation comes from a single fluid.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r1.anchor: فدل على أن الخلق من ماء واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r2.claim: The correct view is that human creation comes from both the man’s and woman’s fluids, because this verse states it explicitly and cannot bear an alternative interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r2.anchor: والصحيح أن الخلق إنما يكون من ماء الرجل والمرأة لهذه الآية فإنها نص لا يحتمل التأويل

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r3.claim: The fluid described as emerging from between the backbone and ribs refers to men’s backbones and women’s ribs, as will be explained later.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r3.anchor: والمراد منه أصلاب الرجال وترائب النساء على ما يأتي بيانه

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r4.claim: Other verses mention water, a fluid, and a drop without assigning them exclusively to either parent; this supports shared parentage, since women emit fluid like men and resemblance derives from both.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r4.anchor: فليس فيه أكثر من أن الله تعالى ذكر خلق الإنسان من الماء والسلالة والنطفة ولم يضفها إلى أحد الأبوين دون الآخر

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r5.claim: Noah’s flood involved rainwater and the earth’s water, since meeting requires two sources; similarly, “a fluid” may mean fluids from both parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r5.anchor: وإنما أراد ماء السماء وماء الأرض لأن الالتقاء لا يكون إلا من اثنين

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r6.claim: One explanation makes shuʿūb the heads of major groupings such as Rabīʿa, Muḍar, Aws, and Khazraj; the singular is shaʿb, named for branching and gathering like tree limbs.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r6.anchor: الشعوب رؤوس القبائل مثل ربيعة ومضر والأوس والخزرج

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r7.claim: The root can mean either gathering or separating: a mishʿab needle joins, while death is called shuʿūb because it separates.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r7.anchor: والشعب من الأضداد يقال شعبته إذا جمعته

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r8.claim: With kasra, shaʿb means a mountain path, plural shiʿāb; al-Jawharī says shaʿb also denotes what branches from Arab or non-Arab tribes.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r8.anchor: فأما الشعب بالكسر فهو الطريق في الجبل والجمع الشعاب

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r9.claim: Al-Shuʿūbiyya is a group that does not rank Arabs above non-Arabs; in a hadith, a man from the shuʿūb means a non-Arab.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r9.anchor: والشعوبية: فرقة لا تفضل العرب على العجم

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a shaʿb is the great tribe that gathers its branches, such as Muḍar, while qabāʾil are its subdivisions.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الشعوب الجمهور مثل مضر. والقبائل الأفخاذ

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r11.claim: One report from Mujāhid says shuʿūb are more distant lineages and qabāʾil nearer ones.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الشعوب البعيد من النسب والقبائل دون ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r12.claim: The root also means to separate; death is called shuʿūb because it divides people.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r12.anchor: وشعبته إذا فرقته، ومنه سميت المنية شعوبا لأنها مفرقة

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r13.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r13.claim: Al-Jawharī says shaʿb is what branches from Arab or non-Arab tribes, with shuʿūb as its plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r13.anchor: قال الجوهري: الشعب: ما تشعب من قبائل العرب والعجم والجمع الشعوب

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r14.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r14.claim: A second report from Mujāhid, also attributed to Qatāda, reverses the distinction: shuʿūb are nearer lineages; al-Māwardī transmits this version.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#3/r14.anchor: وعنه أيضا أن الشعوب النسب الأقرب. وقاله قتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r1.claim: A cited poet says he saw many lineages but none like Saʿd ibn Mālik; another poem says that many tribal groups contain no noble or distinguished person.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r1.anchor: رأيت سعودا من شعوب كثيرة فلم أر سعدا مثل سعد بن مالك

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r2.claim: Other interpretations identify shuʿūb as Yemen’s Qaḥṭān and qabāʾil as Rabīʿa, Muḍar, and other ʿAdnān tribes, or as non-Arab subgroups versus Arab ones.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن الشعوب عرب اليمن من قحطان، والقبائل من ربيعة ومضر وسائر عدنان

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās makes shuʿūb the clients and qabāʾil the Arabs; al-Qushayrī specifies peoples without known ancestry, such as Indians, mountaineers, and Turks.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية: إن الشعوب الموالي، والقبائل العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r4.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī suggests shuʿūb may refer to people associated with regions and routes, while qabāʾil share common ancestry.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r4.anchor: الماوردي: ويحتمل أن الشعوب هم المضافون إلى النواحي والشعاب

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد، ابن الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r5.claim: One hierarchy ranks shaʿb above qabila, faṣīla, ʿimāra, baṭn, and fakhdh; another adds ʿashīra after faṣīla.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r5.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيد عن ابن الكلبي عن أبيه: الشعب أكبر من القبيلة

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r6.claim: Another ordering is shaʿb, qabila, ʿimāra, baṭn, fakhdh, faṣīla, then ʿashīra; poets give mnemonic lists.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r6.anchor: وقيل: الشعب ثم القبيلة ثم العمارة ثم البطن ثم الفخذ ثم الفصيلة ثم العشيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r7.claim: A poet gives shaʿb, qabila, ʿimāra, baṭn, then fakhdh, adding that a youth is sheltered only by his faṣīla.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r7.anchor: وقال آخر: قبيلة قبلها شعب وبعدهما عمارة ثم بطن تلوه فخذ

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r8.claim: The verse reiterates the point made at 43:44: God and His Messenger regard piety, not ancestry, as the criterion.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة «الزخرف» عند قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r9.claim: A reading with fatḥa on an is explained as answering why people should not boast of ancestry: the most honored before God is the most pious, not the best connected.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r9.anchor: كأنه قيل: لم يتفاخر بالأنساب؟ قيل: لأن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r10.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r10.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from Samura that the Prophet said status comes from wealth but nobility from piety; he grades the report ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r10.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن سمرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r11.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r11.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever wishes to be the most honored of people should fear God.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#4/r11.anchor: وقد جاء منصوصا عنه عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r1.claim: Taqwā means observing God’s boundaries in commands and prohibitions, embodying what He ordered and avoiding what He forbade.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r1.anchor: والتقوى معناه مراعاة حدود الله تعالى أمرا ونهيا

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r2.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra quotes God saying He made lineage and made piety the criterion of honor, while people insisted on boasting about ancestors; on Judgment Day God will raise His own lineage and lower theirs, calling for the pious.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r2.anchor: وفي الخبر من رواية أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet’s allies on Judgment Day are the pious, even if another person has closer lineage; people bring deeds while others carry worldly goods and appeal to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r3.anchor: وروى الطبري من حديث أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r4.claim: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet publicly saying that his father’s family are not his allies; his ally is God and the righteous believers.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r4.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل: من أكرم الناس؟

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet first naming Joseph, son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham as most honored, then teaching that the most honored before God is the most pious; the best Arabs in pre-Islamic times are best in Islam if they understand religion.
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r5.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل: من أكرم الناس؟ فقال

QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:49:13#5/r6.speaker: author
